ussenate|ussenate-119-2-81.meaning: A yes vote moved S.J.Res. 138, disapproving a proposed foreign military sale to Israel, out of the Foreign Relations Committee for consideration by the full Senate.

ussenate|ussenate-119-2-83.meaning: A yes vote began Senate consideration of H.J.Res. 140, which would disapprove the Bureau of Land Management's Public Land Order 7917 withdrawing federal lands in Cook, Lake and Saint Louis Counties, Minnesota.

ussenate|ussenate-119-2-85.meaning: A yes vote ended debate (cloture) on the nomination of Andrew B. Davis to be U.S. District Judge for the Western District of Texas.

ussenate|ussenate-119-2-87.meaning: A yes vote began Senate consideration of S.Con.Res. 33, the concurrent resolution setting forth the congressional budget.

ussenate|ussenate-119-2-88.meaning: A yes vote moved S.J.Res. 114, directing removal of U.S. forces from unauthorized hostilities against Iran, out of committee for consideration by the full Senate.

ussenate|ussenate-119-2-89.meaning: A yes vote waived budget rules (3/5 needed) so Schumer Amendment 4799 to the budget resolution, which creates a point of order against reconciliation legislation that does not lower out-of-pocket health care costs, could be considered.

ussenate|ussenate-119-2-9.meaning: A yes vote agreed with a point of order that S.J.Res. 98, on removing U.S. forces from unauthorized hostilities against Venezuela, was not entitled to privileged (expedited) consideration.

ussenate|ussenate-119-2-90.meaning: A yes vote waived budget rules (3/5 needed) so Lujan Amendment 4798 to the budget resolution, which establishes a deficit-neutral reserve fund relating to grocery costs, could be considered.

ussenate|ussenate-119-2-91.meaning: A yes vote waived budget rules (3/5 needed) so Ossoff Amendment 4897 to the budget resolution, which creates a point of order against reconciliation legislation that fails to address insurers delaying or denying care, could be considered.

ussenate|ussenate-119-2-93.meaning: A yes vote waived budget rules (3/5 needed) so Hirono Amendment 4884 to the budget resolution, which creates a point of order against reconciliation legislation not increasing federal funding for or participation in school meal programs, could be considered.

ussenate|ussenate-119-2-94.meaning: A yes vote waived budget rules (3/5 needed) so Hickenlooper Amendment 4956 to the budget resolution, which establishes a deficit-neutral reserve fund on protecting consumers from price increases tied to tariffs and the Iran war, could be considered.

ussenate|ussenate-119-2-95.meaning: A yes vote waived budget rules (3/5 needed) so Alsobrooks Amendment 5294 to the budget resolution, which establishes a deficit-neutral reserve fund relating to increasing child care funding for families, could be considered.

ussenate|ussenate-119-2-96.meaning: A yes vote waived budget rules (3/5 needed) so Kennedy Amendment 5414 to the budget resolution, which sets Rules Committee reconciliation instructions and reserve funds for voter ID, photo ID and election-day ballot counting, could be considered.

ussenate|ussenate-119-2-97.meaning: A yes vote waived budget rules (3/5 needed) so Hawley Amendment 4794 to the budget resolution, which establishes a deficit-neutral reserve fund relating to extending the prohibition on Medicaid payments to abortion providers, could be considered.

ussenate|ussenate-119-2-98.meaning: A yes vote waived budget rules (3/5 needed) so Markey Amendment 5001 to the budget resolution, which creates a point of order against legislation that would not decrease home electricity bills, could be considered.

ussenate|ussenate-119-2-99.meaning: A yes vote adopted Paul Amendment 5378 to the budget resolution, which reduces budget authority in four spending functions to offset $70 billion of new spending, including cutting foreign aid, refugee spending, Education Department and NSF funding.

state-ks-lower|ks-h-20250320-0277_SB137.meaning: Amendment replaces the bill's contents with an exception to the state ban on local firearms regulation, letting cities and counties regulate the sale and purchase of firearms and ammunition inside buildings they own.

state-md-upper|md-26s38.meaning: Amendment changes what a citation to a law enforcement officer for violating the face-covering rule must list: the officer's name and the employing agency's address, instead of the officer's own address.

state-me-lower|me-h77.meaning: Amendment has public defense commission employed counsel and public defenders serve at the executive director's pleasure with pay capped by appropriations, adds requirements for attorney-qualification and caseload rules, and treats deputy district attorneys comparably in pay and benefits.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20250518-7.meaning: Amends the bill to cancel $100 million, instead of $77.2 million, of the Northern Lights Express passenger rail appropriation, and replaces its special education aid reduction with a requirement to increase the special education cross-subsidy aid factor.

state-mn-lower|mn-h-HF0021-20250227-1.meaning: Amends the bill to bar the governor from declaring a new peacetime emergency for the same event if the legislature does not approve the governor's request to extend the emergency.

state-mn-lower|mn-h-HF2434-20250505-1.meaning: Amends the bill to require six affirmative votes, two each from commissioner members, nursing home employer representatives and worker representatives, for the board that sets nursing home employment standards to act, instead of five.

state-mn-lower|mn-h-HF0025-20250313-1.meaning: Amends the bill to remove the conditions barring grantees from using funds to encourage or counsel abortion (unless needed to save the woman's life), provide abortions or refer for them, and barring grants to groups that provide or promote abortion or their affiliates.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260326-2.meaning: Amends the bill to require supportive housing grantee reports 30 days after funds are obligated and every 30 days after, instead of 90, and to include the amount of grant money still unspent.

state-mn-lower|mn-h-HF0001-20250609-1.meaning: Amends the bill so that from Jan. 1, 2026, MinnesotaCare enrollment of undocumented noncitizens is limited to those under 18, over 59, enrolled at any time while under 18, or with a critical health condition such as diabetes or cancer.

state-mn-lower|mn-h-HF0012-20250303-1.meaning: Amends the bill to replace its restriction of girls' teams to females with a requirement that elementary and secondary school athletic programs allow all students to participate consistent with their gender identity or expression.

state-mn-lower|mn-h-HF3295-20260507-1.meaning: Amends the bill to provide that, if a meeting broadcast offers social media comments, comments posted by the public are not government records, are not recorded in minutes, and do not count as public comment; the notice must say they are not public testimony.

state-mn-lower|mn-h-HF3679-20260504-1.meaning: Amends the bill to bar sitting legislators from accepting employment or pay from any nongovernmental organization named as a state funding recipient in a law enacted during their service, with each chamber to adopt enforcement rules.

state-mn-lower|mn-h-HF3682-20260507-1.meaning: Amends the bill to require recipients of state grants of $50,000 or more to certify minimum criteria, including good standing with the secretary of state, current tax filings, and compliance with wage, workers' compensation and unemployment laws.

state-mn-lower|mn-h-HF3732-20260504-1.meaning: Amends the bill to exempt lone employees providing life-protecting services or working with vulnerable adults, and employees during emergencies, from rest and meal break requirements, while still allowing restroom time and time to eat.

state-mn-lower|mn-h-HF0004-20250317-1.meaning: Amends the bill so the tax relief fund surplus is figured from the next biennium's projections for a November forecast in an even-numbered year, and from the current biennium's for a November forecast in an odd-numbered year.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20250609-32.meaning: Amends the bill to create general education disparity aid for districts, based on 0.37 times the gap between a district's per-pupil revenue and the 20th-percentile level, appropriating $17.7 million for fiscal 2026 and $20.8 million for 2027.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260422-14.meaning: Amends the bill to make random drug testing mandatory, rather than optional, for MFIP applicants and participants with a felony drug conviction in the past ten years, and to bar MFIP benefits for 12 months after a positive test.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260505-21.meaning: Amends the bill to bar municipalities from requiring massage therapists, Asian bodywork therapists or unlicensed complementary or alternative health practitioners to be registered with a state health licensing board or the Department of Health.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260512-12.meaning: Amends the bill to count electricity from burning wood chips from timber by-products or discarded wood as carbon-free under the state electricity standard, for technology supplying at least 50% of a utility's annual Minnesota retail sales.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260420-6.meaning: Amends the bill to strike its repeal of a law requiring written consent from owners of two-thirds of nearby property before residential land is rezoned commercial or industrial in first-class cities.

state-mo-upper|mo-s-20260225-01.meaning: Amends the bill to require psychologists, social workers, teachers, law enforcement and certain other professionals to report suspected animal abuse or neglect to a Missouri Animal Control Association hotline within one day, with training and licensing-board penalties.

state-mo-lower|mo-h-20250508-15.meaning: Amends the bill to let cities and counties create civilian police review boards limited to investigating complaints such as excessive force or abuse of authority and recommending discipline; cities of 125,000 to 160,000 residents may grant broader powers.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260421-13.meaning: Amends the bill to require credit unions insured through a commissioner-approved share guaranty corporation to state in statements, advertising and at deposit windows that they are not federally insured, and to obtain members' signed acknowledgment.

state-mn-lower|mn-h-SF1750-20260430-1.meaning: Amends the bill, via an amendment to another amendment, to bar associations and property management companies from selling or disclosing owners' or residents' personal information without an express business purpose, and to require the third party's agreement not to disclose or sell it.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20250506-8.meaning: Amends the bill so the earned sick and safe time law covers only employers with four or more employees, rather than employers with one or more.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20250517-2.meaning: Conference report: Changes cannabis and hemp law, including the Office of Cannabis Management's relationship with Tribal governments, hemp-derived cannabinoid sales, medical cannabis, hemp topicals, license applications, THC limits for beverages, samples at events, and expungement and resentencing of felony cannabis offenses.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20250518-1.meaning: Amends the bill to add state aid payments of $18.8 million to the Teachers Retirement Association and $1.18 million to the St. Paul Teachers Retirement Fund Association.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260407-2.meaning: Amends the bill to bar 340B covered entities from charging uninsured patients, or patients on high-deductible plans, more than the entity's 340B acquisition cost for a prescription drug.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260504-3.meaning: Amends the bill to remove its assault weapon and large-capacity magazine provisions and all its other firearms provisions, including ghost guns, binary triggers and extreme risk protection orders, and to revise its appropriations.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260423-4.meaning: Amends the bill to give each major party caucus leader in the House and Senate access to candidates' street addresses on campaign committee reports, for official business only and without distributing them.

state-nc-upper|nc-S407.meaning: Conference report: Creates a Transylvania County rural development authority, rewrites Boiling Springs' charter, changes Buncombe County sales tax and school capital fund rules, makes Columbus, Gaston, Scotland and Johnston school board elections partisan, and makes other local changes.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260430-8.meaning: Amends the bill to bar business recovery loans to The Quality Learing Center, Inc. (spelled as in the journal), in addition to businesses found guilty of fraud and individuals pardoned for fraud.

state-nc-lower|nc-H15.meaning: Amends the bill to remove the transfer of Department of Public Safety and Department of Information Technology positions to the State Highway Patrol and the reassignment of Archdale Building floors to the Patrol.

state-nc-lower|nc-H686.meaning: Amends the bill to lower the daily virtual currency kiosk transaction limit for new customers from $2,000 to $1,500 and the cap on total fees and spread from 14% to 5% of the transaction.

state-nc-lower|nc-H504.meaning: Amends the bill to provide that citations, fines, penalties, actions and lawsuits pending when the bill's limits on city regulation of U.S. and N.C. flag displays on private property take effect are not abated.

state-nc-upper|nc-S502.meaning: Conference report: removes described property from Southport, Kannapolis and Yadkinville limits, ends Sunset Beach's authority over an extraterritorial area, lets Franklin County acquire land in three adjacent counties, lifts East Spencer's satellite annexation cap, and sets two-year 2026 terms for Forsyth boards.

state-nc-upper|nc-S6.meaning: Amends the bill to add a 14-member study committee on healthcare costs and outcomes that would examine access, state insurance mandates, medical debt, drug prices and regulatory burdens, and recommend legislation by March 31, 2026.

state-nc-lower|nc-H365.meaning: Amends the bill to add studies of on-site child care at every community college and UNC campus (reports due March 31, 2026), of child care centers in State-owned buildings for State employees, and a workgroup on streamlining child care facility licensing requirements.

state-nc-lower|nc-H572.meaning: Conference report: bars public agencies from requiring or publicly releasing personal information identifying members, volunteers or donors of nonprofits, makes it not a public record, allows damages suits and misdemeanor penalties for violations, and lists exceptions such as warrants and legally required reports.

state-nc-lower|nc-H463.meaning: Amends the bill to extend its limits on abuse and neglect petitions and child-abuse charges to parents who raise a child supportively of gender transition, and to bar adoption agencies from denying or delaying placement based on adoptive parents' willingness to support transition.

state-nc-lower|nc-H535.meaning: Amends the bill to remove its provision barring North Carolina IOLTA lawyer trust account interest from being spent on grants or on anything but administrative costs from July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026.

state-nc-upper|nc-S30.meaning: Amends the bill to require the Attorney General to report by June 1, 2025 how many convictions under G.S. 14-277 (impersonation) were obtained from January 2021 through March 1, 2025, and how many involved impersonating an ICE agent.

state-nc-upper|nc-S619.meaning: Conference report: makes many revenue law changes, including moving vapor product directory enforcement to the ALE Division, stronger tax foreclosure collection, rounding cash sales to the nearest five cents once the penny is no longer produced, and tax withholding on certain gaming winnings.

state-nc-upper|nc-S383.meaning: Conference report: requires Charter Schools Review Board approval of charter rules, assigns it certain hearings, puts the executive director under its supervision, lets it hire private counsel, lets large remote academies seek separate charters, and provides $82,100 yearly in lapsed salary funds for it.

state-nc-upper|nc-S510.meaning: Amends the bill to limit its property reappraisal freeze to counties with 15,000 or more people, and to let taxpayers appeal 2026 appraisals in 2026, or in 2027 in counties of that size.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-2-0035.meaning: Amends the bill to require the state's youth camp health and safety rules to mandate that structures used as camper sleeping quarters have air conditioning and heating units as necessary to mitigate extreme temperatures.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-1363.meaning: Amends the bill to require the Texas Future Fund investment policy to prohibit an entity or project that receives an investment from using it to purchase single-family housing.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-4135.meaning: Conference report: Requires people who lobby state officials for a foreign adversary, its clients or its political parties to register as lobbyists and bars them from taking compensation from those parties. Lets the attorney general seek injunctions and civil penalties up to $10,000 per violation.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-0207.meaning: Amends the bill to require businesses receiving money under the Texas technology and innovation program to have at least 75 percent U.S.-citizen employees, and to include in applications the percentage of citizen employees and the immigration status of non-citizen employees.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-1110.meaning: Amends the bill to require a health benefit plan issuer, in its estimate of administrative expenses, to separately report compensation paid to its executive officers, including the chief executive officer and senior executive officers.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-0189.meaning: Amends the bill to require the Texas Cyber Command to adopt policies barring anyone who is not a U.S. citizen from being a member, employee, contractor, volunteer or otherwise affiliated with the command or entities it operates.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250528-031.meaning: Amends the bill to replace its temporary ban on authorizing certain Class V injection wells for aquifer storage with conditions: no more water withdrawn than injected, monitoring wells, water quality testing, data sent to the groundwater district, and a public meeting first.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-2391.meaning: Amends the bill to require a public school where 5 percent or more of admitted students claim a vaccine exemption to give written notice of the school's exemption rate to the parent of each student who claimed a medical exemption.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-2-0051.meaning: Amends the bill to remove its changes to school district budget and tax rate meeting notices (Education Code 44.004) and to limit the remaining notice section to taxing units other than school districts.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-2-0149.meaning: Amends the bill to extend the contribution limit and the ban on travel, food and lodging spending, for legislators absent from the state after arrest warrants issue, to legislative caucuses that also function as special-purpose committees.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-2250.meaning: Amends the bill to make its ban on regulating home-school programs subject to an exception for educational programs paid for with state money distributed under Education Code Chapter 29, Subchapter J.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-2157.meaning: Amends the bill to bar the Teacher Retirement System from implementing its new employer contributions for charter and innovation-plan school staff unless the legislature appropriates enough, beyond required contributions, to cover any resulting increase in unfunded liabilities.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-1906.meaning: Amends the bill to replace its sexually explicit material provisions for municipal libraries with a requirement for a restricted section for material harmful to children, open to adults and to minors with parent or guardian permission.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-1526.meaning: Amends the bill to replace its notice-and-injunction process for structures over 500 feet with a review request to Parks and Wildlife, which recommends measures to minimize harm to migratory birds within 45 days or construction may proceed.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250531-039.meaning: Conference report: Requires assisted living facilities to plan for power outages with climate-controlled refuge areas (15 square feet per resident) or rooms for bedfast residents kept at 68 to 82 degrees, and to notify the state of utility losses over 12 hours.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-0330.meaning: Amends the bill to add website and anonymous-employee options for reporting fraud to the Texas Workforce Commission, an annual report to the legislature on each report received, and a ban on retaliating against employees who report in good faith.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-2256.meaning: Amends the bill to bar the education commissioner, from the 2025-26 through 2027-28 school years, from revoking a district's accreditation, ordering its closure, or imposing interventions or sanctions on districts or charters based on academic performance standards.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-2207.meaning: Amends the bill to require the county commissioners court, as an alternative to other dissolution procedures, to dissolve an industrial development district on petition of owners of a majority of its assessed property value, once its bonds and debts are paid.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-1107.meaning: Amends the bill so that sending reports to the attorney general, and the attorney general's prosecution of trafficking cases, are optional and depend on the local prosecuting attorney's consent, with the attorney general holding concurrent jurisdiction with the local prosecutor.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-2489.meaning: Amends the bill to require providers to give patients the CDC's vaccine information statement or emergency use fact sheet for the COVID-19 vaccine, in place of the state-developed information sheet the bill describes.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250527-038.meaning: Amends the bill to set the penalty for an offense under Election Code Section 64.009, as amended by the bill, at a fine of $550 to $800 plus 10 hours of community service.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-4129.meaning: Conference report: Revises the Texas Space Commission's purposes and board, adding the Economic Development and Tourism Office executive director as a nonvoting member, extends its sunset date from 2032 to 2033, and abolishes the spaceport trust fund.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-1771.meaning: Amends the bill to require a utility using the alternative capital recovery filing to estimate its cost savings, and the Public Utility Commission to reflect a reasonable portion in rates, with residential customers' share of savings at least their share of allocated costs.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-0196.meaning: Amends the bill to require schools to give students in in-school suspension appropriate behavioral support services and educational services comparable to those they would receive in the classroom.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-1608.meaning: Amends the bill to lower the cap on a superintendent's severance payment, and the level above which state funding is reduced, from six months' to four months' salary and benefits.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-1718.meaning: Amends the bill to appropriate $63,750 from the General Revenue Fund for payment of an itemized claim or judgment against the state, to pay Warren Kenneth Paxton Jr. "for salary he did not receive during the period of impeachment."

state-wv-lower|wv-h2026-00360.meaning: Amends the bill to keep the minimum voluntary manslaughter sentence and minimum time before parole eligibility at three years, rather than raising each to five years.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-0051.meaning: Amends the bill to let the legislature tax securities transactions executed as part of high-frequency, algorithmic trading, creating an exception to the bill's ban on taxing securities transactions by registered market operators.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-0155.meaning: Amends the bill to add a rider earmarking $3 million in general revenue within the Texas Broadband Development Office's 2026-27 appropriation to expand broadband in economically distressed and rural communities.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-3276.meaning: Amends the bill to add to the Railroad Commission's annual inactive-well report the failure rates of fluid level and pressure tests by years inactive and district, and the average per-foot-of-depth cost of plugging inactive wells in each district.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-3614.meaning: Amends the bill to drop its perinatal palliative care certification form; instead providers give the pregnant woman the informational materials and provider list and note in her electronic medical record that they were provided.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250424-006.meaning: Amends the bill to make it a third-degree felony for an agent of a foreign government or terrorist organization to spread materially false information to influence opinion or suppress dissent; second degree if aimed at officials, elections, or people by race, religion or immigration status.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-3756.meaning: Amends the bill to create a House select committee, with five members appointed by the Speaker and five from a list from the House Democratic Caucus chair, to study evidence-based firearm risk interventions including extreme risk protective orders.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-3038.meaning: Amends the bill to apply its small-provider measures (simpler grant, reporting and contract requirements in the Thriving Texas Families Program) to providers requesting under $1 million, instead of providers with annual revenue under $2 million.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250428-035.meaning: Amends the bill to let school boards appoint district teachers, counselors and administrators as voting, rather than only nonvoting, members of local school health advisory councils, and removes the bar on those group members being district employees or relatives of employees.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-3608.meaning: Amends the bill to let property owners and tenants sue a city over its occupancy-limit rules for a declaratory judgment, writ of mandamus or injunction, with attorney's fees to a prevailing claimant, in place of the owner damages action.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-3620.meaning: Amends the bill to require that a parcel also be tax delinquent (taxes owed this year and in 5 of the prior 10 years) before a city may declare it abandoned, and to end the process if taxes and penalties are paid by the hearing.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-1861.meaning: Amends the bill to let the governor, after consulting the Department of Public Safety, designate additional countries or entities, including transnational criminal organizations, as barred from buying Texas real property; designations apply only to later purchases.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250410-042.meaning: Amends the bill to keep conduct containing the elements of assault, sexual assault or their aggravated forms as a ground for out-of-school suspension of students below grade three, replacing the bill's "repeated or significant disruption" ground.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-2332.meaning: Amends the bill to let an impact fee increase occur during the bill's three-year freeze if it is a scheduled or stepped increase described in the ordinance, order or resolution that adopted or raised the fee.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-3703.meaning: Amends the bill to bar only people convicted of, or on deferred adjudication for, a felony from serving on a civilian oversight board, removing the bar for those convicted of crimes of moral turpitude.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250512-050.meaning: Amends the bill to require a school district to get a parent's written consent, requested separately and at least 14 days before instruction begins, before a student receives the bill's required fetal development instruction.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-3081.meaning: Amends the bill to require the education commissioner to develop training resources for school administrators on bilingual and dual language programs, expand district reporting on bilingual programs, and require the agency to monitor those programs and assist districts with deficiencies.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250429-005.meaning: Amends the bill to create a teacher student-loan repayment program giving certified teachers with three years' service up to $5,000 a year for five years, plus $2,500 more for bilingual, special education or shortage-area teachers.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250326-020.meaning: Amends the bill to add instruction contrasting communism and fascism with U.S. pluralism and religious freedom, and to cover modern threats posed by fascist as well as communist regimes and ideologies.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-3598.meaning: Amends the bill to limit the attorney general's and Department of Public Safety's authority to enforce the public camping ban to areas within the boundaries of a violating local entity.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-3534.meaning: Amends the bill to replace the required warning labels on foods with 52 listed ingredients with a Texas Tech Health Sciences Center study of the need for and efficacy of a Texas-specific warning label, with a written report due December 1, 2026.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250226-002.meaning: Amends the bill to give each full-time classroom teacher in a district or charter school a $1,000 per school year stipend for personal auto insurance, paid through the Foundation School Program, with the legislature to appropriate the funds.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-3638.meaning: Amends the bill to limit its subdivision-plat exemption for condominiums to cities under Local Government Code Chapter 212, leaving counties' plat rules in place, and to preserve any requirements under Chapter 242.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250429-043.meaning: Amends the bill to remove the requirement that at least 95 percent of the toll revenue a county of 4 million or more people retains be allocated among commissioners precincts by each precinct's share of county-maintained roads.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250601-019.meaning: Conference report: Starts early voting 12 days before elections (9 for May elections), with voting every day including weekends. Requires early-voting sites to also serve on election day. Applies after the Secretary of State reports counties are ready, by August 1, 2027.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250227-002.meaning: Amends the bill so the ban on buying or arranging lottery tickets by phone or internet does not apply to tickets for instant-ticket lottery games.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-3572.meaning: Amends the bill to make the 274th District Court a Comal County-only court from 2027 and remove Comal County from the 22nd District Court from 2029, leaving that court with Caldwell and Hays counties.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-3590.meaning: Amends the bill to make the health care cost evidence it allows parties to offer subject to Texas Rules of Evidence 402 and 403, which limit evidence that is irrelevant or unfairly prejudicial.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-3178.meaning: Amends the bill so discharging a firearm at a habitation, building or vehicle from a motor vehicle is a first-degree felony only if it causes bodily injury or property damage, removing the alternative of placing a person in fear of imminent serious bodily injury.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250312-011.meaning: Amends the bill so a school district or charter school with a state waiver is not in violation of the school-meal food additive ban, and requires the Texas Education Agency to grant a district an automatic one-year waiver on request, once every five years.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250414-007.meaning: Amends the bill so schools and colleges, in deciding whether a student's conduct was motivated by antisemitism, use the state's statutory definition of antisemitism without the examples referenced in it.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250331-025.meaning: Amends the bill to exempt SNAP recipients who live in defined food deserts, meaning high-poverty or low-income areas where many residents live far from a grocery store, from the ban on buying listed items with benefits.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250512-044.meaning: Amends the bill to bar public-accommodation discrimination and add sexual orientation, gender identity and veteran status to state employment and housing anti-discrimination laws, enforced by the Texas Workforce Commission, which may ask the attorney general to sue in pattern-or-practice cases.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-4149.meaning: Conference report: Requires retailers selling alcohol for off-premises use to visually inspect IDs and access their electronic data, with manual entry if a scan fails, bars retaining the data, and bars TABC discipline for sales before September 1, 2027 or during internet outages.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250531-006.meaning: Conference report: Requires sheriffs of counties that run or contract for jails to request and enter federal immigration enforcement agreements, creates a state grant program of $80,000 to $140,000 by county population for participating sheriffs, and lets the attorney general sue noncompliant sheriffs.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250408-010.meaning: Amends the bill so that the duty of school districts, charter schools and their personnel to implement and act in accordance with legally required policies must be carried out 'in good faith'.

state-tx-lower|tx-h-R-3697.meaning: Amends the bill to add to the required campus orientation information on best practices for campus culture and safety as it relates to student organizations, including fraternities and sororities.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250409-027.meaning: Amends the bill to bar insurers from raising a policyholder's annual premium by more than 10% when the prior year's appraisal exceeded the insurer's last offer by 25% or more (not for those with two or more appraisals a year), and to require related rules.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20250417-10.meaning: Amends the bill to remove the section that bars cities with civil service commissions from creating boards for citizen review of law enforcement officers' conduct.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20250417-04.meaning: Amends the bill to require each legislator to take the federal naturalization civics test when a session begins, with each chamber's journal publishing how many questions each member answered correctly.

state-ia-upper|ia-s-20250428-04.meaning: Amends the bill to bar pharmacy benefits managers from limiting pharmacy choice, require 100% of rebates be passed to plan sponsors, set a $10.68 dispensing fee for pharmacies with five or fewer locations, ban spread pricing, and order a report on pharmacy services administrative organizations.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20250513-05.meaning: Amends the bill to raise the FY2026 Resources Enhancement and Protection (REAP) fund appropriation from $12 million to $20 million and to continue the $20 million annual general fund REAP appropriation through 2031 instead of 2028.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20260427-04.meaning: Amends the bill to base deer depredation and shooting permits on economic loss to agriculture, horticulture or silviculture operations from wild animals, rather than listed crop, tree or nursery damage, and changes 2025 dates to 2026.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20250514-06.meaning: Amends the bill to remove the division that lowers the annual cap on Endow Iowa tax credits from $6.5 million to $3.5 million and adds eligibility conditions for the credits.

state-ky-lower|ky-h-25rs-6.meaning: Amends the bill to set 2026 income tax rates at 3.5% on net income up to $90,000, 3.75% from $90,000 to $100,000 and 4% above $100,000, instead of a flat 3.5%, and to remove the annual rate-reduction review process.

state-ky-lower|ky-h-26rs-169.meaning: Amends the bill to let the Medicaid secretary exempt people facing short-term hardship from community engagement requirements, drops the provision continuing them if federal ones end, and requires seeking a hardship waiver for counties with 8.5% or higher unemployment.

state-ky-lower|ky-h-25rs-165.meaning: Amends the bill to require that one of the three Senate-appointed and one of the three House-appointed voting members of the postsecondary education working group be a minority-party member.

state-ky-lower|ky-h-26rs-315.meaning: Amends the bill to require anti-choking devices to be FDA-authorized and limit civil liability immunity to use according to the device's labeled instructions.

state-ky-lower|ky-h-25rs-303.meaning: Amends the bill to add State Police provisions: the commissioner may allow officers to hold law-enforcement-related off-duty jobs and must set policies, including on uniforms, equipment and vehicles used; the police annual-leave provision stays.

state-ky-lower|ky-h-25rs-83.meaning: Amends the bill to delete the definition of "qualified representative" from the occupational safety and health law and remove related references.

state-ky-lower|ky-h-25rs-155.meaning: Amends the bill to limit the definition of "resource" covered by its diversity, equity, and inclusion spending ban to moneys appropriated by the General Assembly.

state-ky-lower|ky-h-26rs-145.meaning: Amends the bill to make tuition waivers for veterans' and first responders' dependents last-dollar awards capped at 128 credit hours and generally ages under 26, and to limit the over-65 waiver to 8 credit hours per semester.

state-ky-lower|ky-h-26rs-309.meaning: Amends the bill to require hiring parties to report their self-employed worker contracts, including number, amount paid and type of portable benefit plans, to the Education and Labor Cabinet, which would issue annual reports with recommendations starting December 1, 2026.

state-ky-lower|ky-h-26rs-319.meaning: Amends the bill to establish that a person may photograph, record, film or observe a first responder if the person does not physically obstruct or threaten the first responder.

state-ky-lower|ky-h-25rs-279.meaning: Amends the bill to let at-home private school students take part in interscholastic athletics at the public school they would be assigned to, and sets conditions and procedures for participation.

state-ky-lower|ky-h-25rs-257.meaning: Amends the bill to set a process for school boards to permit pupils to attend moral instruction, with requests, background checks for instructors and transporters, attendance funding for participants, and repeal of six existing statutes.

state-ky-lower|ky-h-25rs-36.meaning: Amends the bill to state that the resolution does not prevent any organization from donating monuments related to other organized religions for display on the New State Capitol grounds.

state-md-lower|md-26h53.meaning: Amends the bill to bar interpreting or applying it in a way that impairs electric or gas system reliability, emergency response readiness, storm restoration capability, or workforce retention needed to meet PJM, NERC or Commission reliability standards.

state-md-upper|md-26s1095.meaning: Amends the bill to provide that its section on private detention facilities does not apply to the federal government's lease of private land for use as a detention facility.

state-md-lower|md-26h146.meaning: Amends the bill to declare its provisions not severable, so if a court holds any provision or application invalid, no other provision may be given effect.

state-md-lower|md-25h1201.meaning: Amends the bill to bar a person from exercising a right of condemnation in connection with building a solar energy generating station or distributed solar energy generating system under the bill's provisions.

state-md-lower|md-26h421.meaning: Amends the bill to also bar standing in, or otherwise physically occupying, a bus stop zone, and to specify that the stopping, standing or parking ban covers bicycles, electric bicycles and scooters.

state-ma-upper|ma-s56.meaning: Amends the bill to require the Executive Office of Health and Human Services to write regulations on document requests from other states and the federal government, keep a de-identified database of them, and report them annually by December 31 to the legislature's clerks.

state-ma-upper|ma-s64.meaning: Amends the bill to create a voluntary Registry of Motor Vehicles "yellow dot" program for people 62 or older or with a chronic illness. Participants get a window decal and glove-compartment folder with health information for emergency responders; a fee may be charged.

state-ma-upper|ma-s101.meaning: Amends the bill to require the school committee to make a determination within 90 days of the initial complaint.

state-ma-upper|ma-s111.meaning: Amends the bill to change cannabis package labeling rules set by the Cannabis Control Commission, requiring items such as THC content, batch number, ingredients, testing results, a child-warning symbol, and rotating health warnings covering addiction, psychosis and mood disorders.

state-ma-lower|ma-h210.meaning: Amends the bill to let school committees remove school library materials only after a public hearing and a finding, by clear and convincing evidence, that the material has no educational, literary, artistic, personal or social value or is not age appropriate for any student.

state-ma-upper|ma-s125.meaning: Amends the bill to require groups spending $1,000 or more to influence a municipal ballot question to file reports with the municipal clerk: monthly, before the election and after it. Sets penalties up to one year in jail or a $1,000 fine.

state-ma-upper|ma-s135.meaning: Amends the bill to require municipalities and agencies receiving HUD funds to certify annually to the attorney general that they comply with the Fair Housing Act and Title VI, and to send any HUD compliance notice and a corrective plan within 30 days.

state-ma-upper|ma-s138.meaning: Amends the bill to set aside at least $300 million of income surtax revenue each fiscal year for a new Commonwealth K-12 Education Fund, spent on public elementary and secondary education subject to appropriation.

state-ma-upper|ma-s42.meaning: Amends the budget to require licensed innholders of hotels, motels and similar lodgings, and hotels and motels under state emergency housing contracts, to train all employees in human trafficking recognition under an attorney general-approved program. Innholders must post a hotline notice.

state-ma-upper|ma-s156.meaning: Amends the bill to let law enforcement agencies, including police, sheriffs, corrections, courts and probation offices, comply with a federal immigration detainer request for a convicted felon.

state-ma-upper|ma-s204.meaning: Amends the bill to bar gas companies from recovering line extension costs from ratepayers, so new gas customers pay full costs, with exceptions for no feasible alternative, declared critical projects, and certain industrial uses. Tariff changes take effect July 31, 2029.

state-ma-upper|ma-s196.meaning: Amends the bill to let health payers and providers apply to the Health Policy Commission to use an alternative billing and payment system instead of the bill's primary care payment model. The commission decides within 180 days and may approve pilots up to five years.

state-ma-upper|ma-s213.meaning: Amends the bill to bar the chapter 62F tax credit in any fiscal year when net state tax revenues are below 7.5 percent of total statewide personal income, as determined by the Department of Revenue.

state-ma-upper|ma-s180.meaning: Amends the budget to require the University of Massachusetts to study state population changes over the past and next 10 years and their causes and effects, with an advisory panel and at least three public hearings, reporting to legislative clerks by June 30, 2027.

state-wi-upper|wi-sv0206.meaning: Amends the bill to replace the income and franchise tax exemption for broadband expansion grants with a nonrefundable credit equal to 6.32 percent of qualified broadband expansion funding received, for tax years 2026 through 2030.

state-wi-upper|wi-sv0101.meaning: Amends the bill to let parents nominate home-schooled seniors who score at least 33 on the ACT or 1500 on the SAT, for designation as scholars by the Higher Educational Aids Board's executive secretary for the academic excellence higher education scholarship.

state-ct-lower|ct-2025-h-25-hb07066.meaning: Amends the bill to require the education commissioner, with the Connecticut Interscholastic Athletic Conference, to develop guidelines within 15 days for complying with federal Executive Order 14201 on women's sports, and to base school security plan protocols on that guidance.

state-ct-lower|ct-2025-h-28-hb07067.meaning: Amends the bill to raise the additional fiscal 2025 appropriation for the special education Excess Cost grant from $40 million to about $108.2 million.

state-ct-lower|ct-2025-h-30-hb07163.meaning: Amends the bill to replace its contents with a $108.2 million fiscal 2025 General Fund appropriation for the special education Excess Cost grant, provided the April 2025 revenue statement projects a surplus of at least that amount.

state-ct-lower|ct-2025-h-383-hb08002.meaning: Amends the bill to remove the section that would let the Housing commissioner develop housing projects on state-controlled land and sell or lease them, with a right of first refusal for local housing authorities.

state-ct-lower|ct-2026-h-10-sb00299.meaning: Amends the bill to lower the minimum refund value on carbonated and noncarbonated beverage containers from 10 cents to 5 cents, starting July 1, 2026.

state-ct-lower|ct-2026-h-1-sb00083.meaning: Amends the bill to replace it with a "P.L. 119-21 Response Fund" holding $330.8 million: $128 million to offset revenue lost from a new income tax subtraction for overtime and tip income, and $202.8 million to the Office of Policy and Management.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20250422-05.meaning: Amends the bill to let local governments set up length of service award programs for volunteer firefighters, EMS volunteers and reserve peace officers, with state matching grants up to $500 per recipient per year, funded by $1.5 million from sports wagering receipts.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20260502-03.meaning: Amends the bill to remove the section requiring HHS to employ dedicated central-office staff to identify and notify relatives of children removed from parental custody, leaving the rule on placing children with licensed foster parents.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20250423-05.meaning: Amends the bill to set an effective date of January 1, 2026.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20250424-03.meaning: Amends the bill to bar price discrimination between grocery stores in and out of the grocer reinvestment program when it may substantially lessen competition or create a monopoly, while allowing price differences that reflect cost differences.

state-ia-upper|ia-s-20260502-08.meaning: Amends the bill to change two five-year civil filing periods to fifty years: the period for minors to file claims after reaching adulthood, and the period to sue over child sexual abuse or human trafficking after discovering the injury.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20250513-13.meaning: Amends the bill to add an inclusive-environment goal and a review of state laws affecting workforce retention, and to raise appropriations for the rent subsidy program ($873,000 to $1.5 million), misclassification investigations ($382,685 to $600,000) and the grocer fund ($1.25 million to $2 million).

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20250130-01.meaning: Amends the bill to keep the rule that National Guard scholarship eligibility and awards cannot depend on a member's unit, drill location, or Army versus Air National Guard membership, which the bill otherwise strikes.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20260317-03.meaning: Amends the bill to replace scheduling kratom as a controlled substance with rules requiring product registration, lab testing, labeling with a 21-and-over warning, and a 25 mg per serving cap on 7-hydroxymitragynine; processor violations are serious misdemeanors.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20260226-16.meaning: Amends the bill to add county supervisors, city council members and school board members to the officials who can request that their names be redacted from county assessor and recorder documents posted online.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20260225-08.meaning: Amends the bill to let counties and cities issue identification cards to residents if each card states that it is not intended to serve as an official identifying document.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20260312-17.meaning: Amends the bill to require state entities and public colleges to reimburse the attorney general's special counsel costs only if they are found to have violated the chapter's restrictions.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20260303-12.meaning: Amends the bill to add the impact on public and nonpublic schools to the Department of Education's annual report on area education agency changes under 2024 Iowa Acts, chapter 1002.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20260303-22.meaning: Amends the bill to exempt citizens of NATO member nations from the Board of Regents policy barring employment contracts with H-1B visa holders who are citizens of federally designated foreign adversary nations.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20260304-24.meaning: Amends the bill to limit habitual offender status to people currently convicted of a level one forcible felony who have prior convictions worth at least two points, for three or more points in total.

state-ia-upper|ia-s-20260401-03.meaning: Amends the bill to require a treatment plan within 24 hours of admission to subacute mental health facilities, set 48-hour to 10-day deadlines for prior-authorization decisions, create a bed-tracking system for children's psychiatric institutions, and order a rules review.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20260224-03.meaning: Amends the bill to require the Board of Regents to report by its November 2026 meeting on how it could set up performance-based funding using graduation rates, high-demand degrees, post-graduation employment and income, and graduates who stay in Iowa.

state-ia-upper|ia-s-20260407-07.meaning: Amends the bill to set the bond a grain dealer without an audited financial statement must file for credit-sale contracts at $100,000 for deferred-payment and $300,000 for deferred-pricing contracts, and to limit how grain indemnity fund money may be spent.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20260304-05.meaning: Amends the bill to make the court text-notification system opt-in instead of opt-out, so people cited or arrested, victims, witnesses, and attorneys receive notifications only if they choose to enroll.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20250227-02.meaning: Amends the bill to remove its sections that would delete "gender identity" and its definition from the Iowa Civil Rights Act's employment and pay provisions and from the state job-posting nondiscrimination statement, leaving current law in place.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20260303-15.meaning: Amends the bill to remove its division that would let school districts move unspent teacher salary supplement funds into their general fund flexibility accounts.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20260408-12.meaning: Amends the bill to add rules for proprietary onsite wastewater treatment systems: maintenance contracts with certified technicians renewed annually or biannually, annual or twice-yearly inspections, reports to the DNR with a public database, and a DNR study with a report due January 10, 2028.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20260408-04.meaning: Amends the bill to replace it with a fee on wire transmissions to or from locations abroad: $5 per transmission plus 2 percent of any amount above $500, with 90 percent going to the human trafficking office and 10 percent to the general fund.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20260502-18.meaning: Amends the bill to raise the victim assistance grants appropriation in the proposed replacement text from about $5.54 million to about $6.18 million.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20260501-03.meaning: Amends the bill to appropriate $600,000 a year from the groundwater protection fund to the University of Iowa for the Iowa Water Quality Information System, replacing the $300,000 one-year amount in the proposed text.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20260502-47.meaning: Amends the bill to remove its division that changes the 2023 National Electrical Code for Iowa homes (such as dropping arc-fault interrupter requirements) and bars local electrical codes stricter than the national code.

state-ia-upper|ia-s-20250408-03.meaning: Amends the bill to let residents of the nursing facility, as well as facility representatives, provide context or evidence in the department's review of a deficient practice before final findings of immediate jeopardy or substandard quality of care.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20250318-26.meaning: Amends the bill to move the tuition decision deadline from December 31 to April 30, drop the 3 percent tuition cap and the first-year tuition guarantee (replaced by a study), and soften the three-year degree and work-study requirements.

state-ia-upper|ia-s-20250512-06.meaning: Amends the bill to set rules for permits for electric power plants, transmission lines, and pipelines, including commissioners attending hearings, objection filing, operator liability for drainage tile and crop damage, and farmland restoration standards.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20250313-03.meaning: Amends the bill to drop the exclusion of vaccinations from the preventative care the Department of Health and Human Services may consent to as routine medical care for children in its custody.

state-ia-upper|ia-s-20250417-05.meaning: Amends the bill to make information from legislative branch security camera systems and from state employee ID card building access systems confidential under the open records law.

state-ky-lower|ky-h-25rs-274.meaning: Amends the bill to bar the state board from approving a school of innovation request that uses an education service provider banned from providing education services in another state.

state-ky-lower|ky-h-25rs-271.meaning: Amends the bill to require each executive department and program cabinet to report to the Legislative Research Commission twice a year with cost-saving measures, functions that could be eliminated, and staff positions that could be eliminated or converted.

state-ky-lower|ky-h-26rs-432.meaning: Amends the bill to remove the section designating Kentucky Route 18 in Boone County as the "Charlie Kirk Memorial Highway."

state-ma-lower|ma-h21.meaning: Amends the bill to replace proposed House rule 85A with a rule that audits of the House be conducted by the State Auditor under section 11 of chapter 12 of the General Laws.

state-ma-lower|ma-h39.meaning: Amends the bill to bar the housing office and the Attorney General from enforcing any MBTA Communities zoning law (chapter 40A, section 3A) requirement before December 31, 2026.

state-ma-lower|ma-h63.meaning: Amends the bill to redefine "legally protected health care activity" to cover reproductive and gender-affirming care and aiding others, plus refusing to obtain such or other preventive care for oneself or minor children, excluding care below professional standards or violating anti-discrimination laws.

state-ma-upper|ma-s105.meaning: Amends the bill to state that the resolution's rescission of all prior Article V convention applications supersedes them "into perpetuity."

state-ma-lower|ma-h120.meaning: Amends the bill to create, subject to appropriation, a Massachusetts AED Communities Fund run by the Department of Public Health to help cities and towns pay for defibrillators and related equipment.

state-ma-lower|ma-h123.meaning: Amends the bill to move state primaries from the seventh to the eleventh Tuesday before biennial state elections.

state-ma-lower|ma-h143.meaning: Amends the bill to require a yearly transfer of the greater of $100 million or 50% of the prior-year balance into a new fund distributed to cities and towns by population for roads, bridges and school facilities.

state-ma-lower|ma-h147.meaning: Amends the bill to define "law enforcement agency" and "officer" in its immigration provisions to include sheriffs' departments, college, hospital and humane society police, special and deputy sheriffs, constables making arrests, and reserve officers.

state-ma-lower|ma-h152.meaning: Amends the bill to provide that state student device policy laws do not require school districts to incur new costs, while letting districts adopt policies that cost more.

state-ma-lower|ma-h214.meaning: Amends the bill to bar distribution of the $22.5 million No Cost Call Trust Fund transfer until the budget secretary presents a plan to keep annual spending from the item under $10 million.

state-ma-lower|ma-h173.meaning: Amends the bill to give state, county and municipal public health and safety workers who worked in person during the COVID-19 emergency a retirement credit equal to its length (March 2020 to June 2021), with local governments opting in.

state-ma-lower|ma-h12.meaning: Amends the bill to replace the Senate version with $425 million for homeless family shelter, disclosure of convictions and pending serious charges by adult applicants, a six-month eligibility cap with hardship waivers, and 30-day temporary respite stays.

state-ma-upper|ma-s22.meaning: Amends the bill to require the Clerk to mark "Virtual Vote (VV)" beside any senator's name in published roll calls when the senator votes by remote participation.

state-ma-upper|ma-s6.meaning: Amends the bill to require a yeas-and-nays recorded vote on all conference committee reports.

state-ma-upper|ma-s51.meaning: Amends the bill to strike section 41, which changes how electric companies recover costs for added distribution infrastructure, including deeming applications approved if the utilities department does not act within six months.

state-md-lower|md-26h422.meaning: Amends the bill to exclude from the definition of a shielded record any record of a landlord's action against a tenant for damage beyond ordinary wear and tear to the premises, common areas, major appliances, or furnishings.

state-md-upper|md-25s1247.meaning: Amends the bill to require every municipality to require voter registration for its elections, bar noncitizens from registering to vote in municipal elections, and remove the exemption for municipalities that do not require voter registration.

state-md-lower|md-25h264.meaning: Amends the bill to start the rental air-conditioning requirement on October 1, 2025 instead of June 1, covering newly constructed units and units undergoing a renovation of electrical or heating systems.

state-md-lower|md-26h217.meaning: Amends the bill to require valuing commercial and multifamily property within one mile of a Metro station in Montgomery and Prince George's counties, after June 2028, to yield at least $140 million in State property tax, sent to the Transportation Trust Fund.

state-md-lower|md-25h445.meaning: Amends the bill to remove its reduced penalties for cannabis volume dealing (50 pounds or more) and cannabis drug kingpin offenses, keeping current law's mandatory minimum sentences for both.

state-md-lower|md-26h25.meaning: Amends the bill to replace Maryland's legislative district standards with new standards for legislative and congressional districts, including respect for political boundaries and bans on considering voter registration, past votes, party, or any individual's residence, including incumbents'.

state-md-lower|md-25h970.meaning: Amends the bill to exempt Baltimore County from the bill's requirements if the county completes its comprehensive zoning map process at least every five years.

state-md-lower|md-26h338.meaning: Amends the bill to require county boards to notify parents of students in schools rated one star for three years and offer alternative schools, create nonpublic school scholarships, and have school systems pay for military boarding school for students deemed violent or repeatedly disciplined.

state-md-lower|md-26h1067.meaning: Amends the bill to make theft of a firearm a felony: up to 5 years or a $1,000 fine for a first conviction, up to 10 years or $2,500 after, served consecutively to any other sentence.

state-md-lower|md-25h266.meaning: Amends the bill to start the three-year limit for local consumer protection enforcement when the violation was committed, instead of when local authorities knew or should have known of it.

state-md-lower|md-25h451.meaning: Amends the bill to exclude from the tax program any individual convicted of, or who pleaded guilty to, a tax-related crime.

state-md-upper|md-26s1075.meaning: Amends the bill to replace the Muslim American Heritage and Jewish American Heritage months with a single All Religions Month, which the Governor must proclaim each April.

state-md-lower|md-26h339.meaning: Amends the bill to bar local governments from setting housing construction permit requirements stricter than state requirements unless state law expressly allows it, and to require a justification to the State Housing Ombudsman and Legislative Policy Committee when a stricter rule reduces housing supply.

state-md-lower|md-26h1219.meaning: Amends the bill to exempt 16 listed federal installations in Maryland, including Aberdeen Proving Ground, Fort Meade and the Naval Academy, from the bill's reservation of state jurisdiction over federal land.

state-md-lower|md-25h588.meaning: Amends the bill to change its rule on waiving the right to reclaim property after an eviction: if the landlord and tenant agree on a date and time for the tenant to reclaim it, the tenant may waive that right. The bill had barred waiver.

state-md-lower|md-26h1016.meaning: Amends the bill to provide that local good cause lease termination laws may not apply to a landlord who is an active service member.

state-md-lower|md-25h610.meaning: Amends the bill to bar the Public Service Commission from issuing a certificate of public convenience and necessity for an overhead transmission line until the governing body of each county the line would cross has approved its construction.

state-md-upper|md-25s909.meaning: Amends the bill to also exclude from sentence-reduction motions anyone convicted of murder of a probation officer who was performing official duties when killed.

state-md-upper|md-26s541.meaning: Amends the bill to limit the panel that nominates Maryland Parole Commission members to seven: the police training director, public safety secretary, Public Defender, State's Attorneys' Association president and three Governor-appointed service providers, dropping the other panel seats.

state-md-upper|md-25s775.meaning: Amends the bill to lower, from 5% to 2%, the share of an existing priority preservation area's acreage that may host solar stations; the bill's prohibitions then stop applying to the remaining 98%.

state-md-upper|md-25s646.meaning: Amends the bill to exempt people convicted of criminal organization (gang) offenses under Title 9, Subtitle 8 of the Criminal Law Article from its limits on sharing personal information, records and database information for immigration enforcement.

state-sc-lower|sc-h-26194.meaning: Amends the bill to bar state-supported colleges, public school districts and charter school districts from receiving appropriated funds if they require students to show proof of COVID-19 vaccination for enrollment, on-campus instruction or on-campus residence.

state-sc-lower|sc-h-26705.meaning: Amends the bill to require emergency medical care providers to make a reasonable effort to ensure a parent, guardian or appropriate family member has consented to medical treatment as provided by law.

state-sc-lower|sc-h-27062.meaning: Amends the bill to apply its noncompete provisions only to hospitals owned and operated by the State.

state-sc-upper|sc-s-25602.meaning: Amends the bill to replace it with a package changing joint-and-several liability and verdict-form rules, setting when alcohol sellers are liable for serving intoxicated patrons, requiring alcohol server certification, and barring insurer bad-faith claims when policy limits are paid on deadline.

state-sc-lower|sc-h-27478.meaning: Amends the bill to add de-escalation and restraint training to the classroom-management guidance the Department of Education must develop for school districts and educator preparation programs.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20250313-12.meaning: Amends the bill to specify that "private information" does not include the name or license number of a person licensed by the department of inspections, appeals, and licensing or a licensing board under it.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20250318-10.meaning: Amends the bill to remove the process for a parent to petition for a student to keep a personal electronic device during class for health reasons, and to add students with an individual health plan on file to those who keep access.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20250318-14.meaning: Amends the bill so the new requirement to screen kindergarten through grade 6 students in mathematics and intervene for those persistently at risk applies to school years beginning on or after July 1, 2026.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20250326-11.meaning: Amends the bill to require each charter school governing board member to follow the same ban on interests in school contracts that applies to school district board members.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20250326-23.meaning: Amends the bill to strike the provision requiring the department to discontinue the Iowa health and wellness plan, or allowing an alternative plan, if federal law no longer allows work requirements (via an amendment to amendment H-1195).

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20250512-07.meaning: Amends the bill to replace the appropriation of Gadsden flag plate fees to public safety for firearm training grants with an appropriation to health and human services for programs assisting employed people with permanent disabilities.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20250514-11.meaning: Amends the bill so its unemployment tax changes apply only to employers that sign an agreement with the department not to outsource jobs from Iowa work sites to other countries, and only during the agreement term.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20250417-17.meaning: Amends the bill to require applicants for an anaerobic digester construction permit to consent to state testing of digester structure materials for PFAS chemicals (via an amendment to amendment H-1230).

state-ia-upper|ia-s-20250318-02.meaning: Amends the bill to remove the exemption for people operating an implement of husbandry from its restriction on using electronic devices while driving.

state-ia-upper|ia-s-20260223-07.meaning: Amends the bill to also require excused absences for any bona fide activity approved by the federal Department of Education, including career and technical student organizations, in addition to 4-H and FFA activities.

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20260331-03.meaning: Amends the bill to make employing commercial drivers lacking sufficient English proficiency a simple misdemeanor with a $10,000 scheduled fine per violation, instead of a serious misdemeanor with up to one year in jail (via an amendment to amendment H-8265).

state-ia-lower|ia-h-20260502-31.meaning: Amends the bill to keep oil and gas well data confidential for one year (basic data) or three years (interpretive data) from the spud date, each extendable one year, and to require producers to file well logs and reports within 120 days.

state-ia-upper|ia-s-20261002-02.meaning: Amends the bill to require businesses receiving major economic growth attraction program incentives to stay neutral in any labor union organizing effort for the agreement term and maintenance period.

state-md-lower|md-25h587.meaning: Amends the bill to require the Department of the Environment to adopt regulations for ecological restoration of decommissioned ground-mounted solar facilities.
