state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260429-17.meaning: A yes vote would have added to HF 4188's nudification provisions a gross misdemeanor penalty for intentionally nudifying an image or video of a non-consenting person, and labeled the existing penalties as civil.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260429-18.meaning: A yes vote passed HF 4188, as amended, the commerce policy bill modifying insurance and financial product consumer protections, prohibiting virtual-currency kiosks, and revising securities broker-dealer and unclaimed property provisions.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260429-21.meaning: A yes vote would have added to HF 1606, which prohibits access to nudification technology, a gross misdemeanor for intentionally nudifying an image or video of a non-consenting person, and labeled its existing penalties as civil.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260429-25.meaning: A yes vote would have barred charging a storage fee under HF 4075's firearm-restriction procedure to anyone who, in the past year, qualified for a public defender or was approved to proceed in forma pauperis.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260429-3.meaning: A yes vote adopted Senator Dibble's amendment (A47) so SF 4612's limit of medical assistance to federally eligible noncitizens also excepts people served by a nonprofit torture-victim center, alongside pregnant noncitizens.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260429-4.meaning: A yes vote adopted Senator Boldon's amendment (A51) adding to SF 4612 a medical assistance policy of ending duplicative requirements mandated by section 71119 of Public Law 199-21 (as printed) for the Affordable Care Act expansion population.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260429-5.meaning: A yes vote adopted Senator Dibble's amendment (A49) adding people diagnosed with HIV or AIDS to the list of medically frail people exempt from SF 4612's work or community engagement requirement.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260429-6.meaning: A yes vote adopted Senator McEwen's amendment (A101) adding to SF 4612 a requirement that a successor health care entity offer eligible employees 120 days of continued employment at no lower pay, with severance, unless it assumes the union contract.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260429-7.meaning: A yes vote adopted an amendment striking "provided to undocumented noncitizens" from Senator Lucero's proposed addition to SF 4612's Hennepin Healthcare reporting list, leaving a requirement to report total charity care spending.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260429-8.meaning: A yes vote sustained the President's ruling that Senator Lucero's amendment (A104) to his A79 amendment to SF 4612, adding "expended on illegal immigrants," was out of order.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260429-9.meaning: A yes vote would have made Hennepin Healthcare eligible for an SF 4612 grant only if it stopped spending on diversity, equity, and inclusion initiatives and on climate change, climate justice, and sustainability initiatives.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260430-11.meaning: A yes vote would have added "and not an illegal alien" to Senator Lucero's A25 amendment requiring owners of businesses eligible for SF 4535 recovery loans to have lawful immigration status.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260430-12.meaning: A yes vote would have required the permanent-resident owners of businesses eligible for SF 4535's business recovery loans to have lawful immigration status.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260430-13.meaning: A yes vote would have deleted SF 4535's loan forgiveness subdivision, which lets borrowers with 24 consecutive on-time payments apply for forgiveness of up to 60 percent of the loan.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260430-14.meaning: A yes vote would have required 36 rather than 24 consecutive on-time payments, and lowered the forgivable share from 60 to 50 percent of the loan, in SF 4535's loan forgiveness provision.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260430-15.meaning: A yes vote passed SF 4535, as amended, which establishes a Minnesota business recovery loan program, cancels prior appropriations, appropriates and transfers money, and requires a report.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260430-4.meaning: A yes vote adopted Senator Champion's amendment (A51) changing Senator Kreun's SF 4535 amendment from requiring five percent of program money for Legislative Auditor or BCA fraud oversight to allowing up to five percent.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260430-5.meaning: A yes vote adopted Senator Champion's amendment (A52) specifying that the economic development commissioner must authorize up to five percent of SF 4535 program money for Legislative Auditor or BCA fraud oversight.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260430-7.meaning: A yes vote would have expanded SF 4535's $250,000 economic analysis of increased immigration enforcement to also cover fraudulent payments from state-administered programs since January 7, 2019.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260430-9.meaning: A yes vote would have added The Quality Learing Center, Inc. (as spelled in the journal) to the Champion (A53) amendment barring SF 4535 loans to businesses found guilty of fraud or individuals pardoned for fraud.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260505-1.meaning: A yes vote would have replaced subdivision 8 of SF 4059 with a $300,000 competitive grant program for cross-training medical personnel to keep rural hospital maternity units open.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260505-10.meaning: A yes vote would have deleted from SF 4059 a $200,000 suitable seating enforcement appropriation and the labor policy article, which includes a requirement that employers provide suitable seating.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260505-11.meaning: A yes vote would have added to SF 4059's labor policy article a definition of "employer" as an art center founded before 1880 in a city of the first class.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260505-13.meaning: A yes vote sustained the President's ruling that Drazkowski's A53 amendment to his A45 amendment to SF 4059, which would have made legislators pay half of their paid family leave premiums, was not germane.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260505-14.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Bahr's A54 amendment to SF 4059, as amended, banning legislator per diem payments during regular session and barring legislator compensation beyond salary, insurance, retirement and listed expenses, effective July 1, 2027.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260505-15.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Draheim's A40 amendment to SF 4059, as amended, requiring executive agencies to build zero-based budgets on a ten-year schedule and have forecast and base spending treated as zero in their scheduled year.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260505-16.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Draheim's A44 amendment to SF 4059, requiring the attorney general to report each January 15 on the Medicaid Fraud Control Unit's budget, spending, cases and outcomes and present it to committees on request.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260505-17.meaning: A yes vote sustained the President's ruling that Duckworth's A55 amendment to SF 4059, which would have voided limits on displaying POW/MIA, armed forces, Blue Star and Gold Star flags at residences, was not germane.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260505-19.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Kreun's A30 amendment to SF 4059, changing Minn. Stat. 13.65, subd. 1 so the listed Attorney General Office data are classified as private only when they are data on individuals.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260505-2.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Nelson's A29 amendment to SF 4059, the Preserving Girls Sports Act, limiting female school athletic teams to those female at birth and appropriating $50,000 to the Minnesota State High School League.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260505-20.meaning: A yes vote passed SF 4059, as amended, the omnibus state government finance bill appropriating money for education, environment, energy, jobs, labor, public safety and state government, in the Senate.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260505-22.meaning: A yes vote passed SF 3298, as amended, which changes licensing and scope of practice for several health occupations, sets massage therapist registration and music therapist licensure, and creates advisory councils.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260505-3.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Rarick's A31 amendment to SF 4059, having Minnesota join the federal scholarship-granting organization tax credit (Public Law 119-21, sec. 70411), defining qualifying organizations and conforming state tax law.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260505-5.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Green's A20 amendment to SF 4059, changing the definitions of exempt materials and paper product in Minnesota's packaging producer-responsibility law (Minn. Stat. 115A.1441).

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260505-6.meaning: A yes vote sustained the President's ruling that Lang's A101 amendment to SF 4059, which would have raised the all-terrain vehicle dry weight limit from 2,000 to 3,500 pounds, was not germane.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260505-7.meaning: A yes vote adopted Hauschild's A19 amendment to SF 4059, letting holders of timber permits expiring May 1 to July 31, 2026 request a one-year extension from the DNR commissioner without penalty or interest.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260505-8.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Green's A21 amendment to SF 4059, deleting the bill's article 7, the renewable development finance article.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260505-9.meaning: A yes vote adopted Rarick's A28 amendment to SF 4059, cutting the administrative-cost caps for the supplemental energy assistance grant program from 12.5% to 3.5%, Commerce's share from 2.5% to 0.75%, and outreach from 5% to 1.5%.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260506-11.meaning: A yes vote passed HF 3709, as amended, which allows certain virtual-currency custody services to be offered and performed; the amendment replaced 'fiduciary' with 'custodial' wording.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260506-3.meaning: A yes vote would have amended the Frentz (A50) amendment to SF 4476 so it struck bill sections 28 to 34, including assisted living nursing staffing rules and rules on for-profit takeovers of nonprofit nursing homes and assisted living facilities.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260506-4.meaning: A yes vote adopted the Frentz (A50) amendment to SF 4476, striking the bill's nursing home staffing standards (onsite registered nurse, 3.48 nursing hours per resident), the matching assisted living staffing rule and a repealer, and adjusting appropriations.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260506-5.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Pratt's A45 amendment to SF 4476, repealing the increase of the nursing home license surcharge to $5,900 per bed and cutting the rate surcharge component from $19.02 to $8.86 per resident day.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260506-6.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Rasmusson's A43 amendment to SF 4476, letting a nursing home's or assisted living facility's controlling owners ask the health commissioner to take over operation through a receiver.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260506-7.meaning: A yes vote sustained the President's ruling that Rasmusson's A47 amendment to SF 4476, which would have set pay at 75% for agency heads awaiting Senate confirmation, was not germane.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260506-8.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Gruenhagen's A49 amendment to SF 4476, requiring termination of the human services commissioner within 30 days if improperly paid medical assistance claims in a year exceed 2% of the department's budget.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260506-9.meaning: A yes vote passed SF 4476, as amended, the omnibus human services supplemental bill covering continuity of care, aging and disability services, behavioral health, and long-term care facility regulation, in the Senate.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260507-3.meaning: A yes vote passed HF 1141, as amended, the housing finance and policy bill, in the Senate.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260507-4.meaning: A yes vote adopted Duckworth's A-2 amendment to HF 3900, requiring a two-thirds vote of each house to pass a law on permanent school fund distribution policy or apportionment among school districts.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260507-7.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Westrom's A-1 amendment to HF 3521, replacing it with a full repeal of the hospital construction moratorium (Minn. Stat. 144.551) while keeping conditions of past exceptions in effect.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260511-10.meaning: A yes vote passed SF 3699, as amended, which restricts immigration enforcement at sensitive locations, creates civil remedies, and changes the concealing identity crime and use of force investigations.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260511-12.meaning: A yes vote adopted Heintzeman's A-2 amendment to HF 3426, deleting the $1,252,000 trust fund appropriation to the DNR for an agreement with Friends of the Boundary Waters Wilderness (Cultivating Conservation Leaders).

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260511-13.meaning: A yes vote passed HF 3426, as amended, which appropriates money from the environment and natural resources trust fund and modifies trust fund and community grant program provisions.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260511-4.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Holmstrom's A-3 amendment to HF 4252, barring undocumented or not lawfully present noncitizens from state-funded financial aid from the commissioner, starting with fall 2026 awards.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260511-5.meaning: A yes vote passed HF 4252, as amended, the higher education finance and policy bill, in the Senate.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260511-6.meaning: A yes vote adopted Latz's A11 amendment to SF 3699, revising its limits on civil immigration enforcement at courts, health care facilities and schools, including good-faith employee liability limits and an earlier school date, December 31, 2026.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260511-7.meaning: A yes vote sustained the President's ruling that Kreun's A10 amendment to the Kreun (A-9) amendment to SF 3699, a full substitute for the bill, was not germane.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260511-8.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Kreun's A52 amendment to his A-9 amendment, replacing SF 3699 with a substitute banning local ordinances limiting immigration enforcement, creating a civil rights cause of action, and staying releases on ICE detainers.

state-mn-upper|mn-s-20260511-9.meaning: A yes vote adopted Kreun's A-9 amendment to SF 3699, removing the civil-arrest protection for people on any public way within 1,000 feet of a courthouse while attending court proceedings.

state-nc-upper|nc-S444.meaning: A yes vote adopted an amendment to HB 87 that deleted the word "State" from the bill's reference to the "North Carolina State Constitution" (Senator Hise).

state-nc-upper|nc-S445.meaning: A yes vote adopted an amendment to HB 87 requiring the State Education Assistance Authority to set any necessary rules by July 1, 2026, or within 120 days of federal regulations, whichever is later.

state-nc-upper|nc-S446.meaning: A yes vote tabled (set aside) an amendment to HB 87 that would have made the act take effect only once the State fully funds free and reduced-price meals for qualifying public school students.

state-nc-upper|nc-S447.meaning: A yes vote tabled (set aside) an amendment to HB 87 that would have made the act take effect only once the State fully funds special education in public schools.

state-nc-upper|nc-S448.meaning: A yes vote tabled (set aside) an amendment to HB 87 that would have added an individual income tax credit for donations to public elementary and secondary schools.

state-nc-upper|nc-S449.meaning: A yes vote tabled (set aside) an amendment to HB 87 that would have barred scholarship granting organizations from awarding scholarships to immediate family members of their donors.

state-nc-upper|nc-S450.meaning: A yes vote tabled (set aside) an amendment to HB 87 that would have added an individual income tax credit for donations to disaster relief organizations serving North Carolina.

state-nc-upper|nc-S463.meaning: A yes vote tabled (set aside) an amendment to HB 926 that would have kept the bill's flag-ordinance provision from abating citations, fines and proceedings already pending when it takes effect.

state-nc-upper|nc-S471.meaning: A yes vote tabled (set aside) an amendment that would have deleted Sections 1.2 through 1.9 of HB 562, including the LME/MCO transfers, DHHS position eliminations and Medicaid audit, and conforming title language.

state-nc-upper|nc-S480.meaning: A yes vote adopted an amendment to HB 307 making lethal injection the default execution method, with the Secretary of Adult Correction selecting another method if it is declared unconstitutional or unavailable.

state-nc-upper|nc-S482.meaning: A yes vote tabled (set aside) an amendment to HB 307 that would have moved $70 million from NCInnovation to fund grants to sheriffs' offices for jail staffing, overcrowding and detainee mental health care.

state-nc-upper|nc-S486.meaning: A yes vote tabled (set aside) an amendment to SB 249 that would have replaced the bill's congressional map with a different 14-district map offered by Senator Mohammed.

state-nc-upper|nc-S488.meaning: A yes vote tabled (set aside) an amendment to SB 249 that would have required the State Board of Elections to notify every voter affected by the new map of their congressional district by December 1, 2025.

state-nc-upper|nc-S489.meaning: A yes vote tabled (set aside) an amendment to SB 249 that would have required county boards of elections to hold at least four hours of early voting on one Sunday at each early voting site.

state-nc-upper|nc-S490.meaning: A yes vote tabled (set aside) an amendment to SB 249 that would have allowed a ten-day grace period for returning absentee ballots postmarked on Election Day.

state-nc-upper|nc-S491.meaning: A yes vote would have tabled SB 249, the congressional redistricting bill, on second reading, setting the bill aside without a vote on passage.

state-nc-upper|nc-S532.meaning: A yes vote tabled (set aside) an amendment to SB 1080 that would have eliminated state income tax for individuals earning less than the State's median income.

state-nc-upper|nc-S533.meaning: A yes vote tabled (set aside) an amendment to SB 1080 that would have exempted the top one percent of earners from the proposed constitutional cap on the state income tax rate.

state-nc-upper|nc-S536.meaning: A yes vote tabled (set aside) an amendment to SB 1082 that would have replaced its text with a constitutional $15 State minimum wage beginning January 1, 2028, indexed to inflation.

state-nc-upper|nc-S537.meaning: A yes vote tabled (set aside) an amendment to SB 1082 that would have removed "or nonmembership" so the measure protected only employment while a member of a labor union or association.

state-nc-upper|nc-S538.meaning: A yes vote tabled (set aside) an amendment to SB 1082 that would have replaced its text with a constitutional right of public employees, including first responders, to collectively bargain.

state-nc-upper|nc-S539.meaning: A yes vote tabled (set aside) an amendment to SB 1082 that would have replaced its text with a constitutional policy that employers provide paid medical, sick and family leave and breaks.

state-nc-upper|nc-S540.meaning: A yes vote tabled (set aside) an amendment to SB 1082 that would have let local governments set a higher minimum wage and require paid sick days and family leave policies.

state-nc-upper|nc-S541.meaning: A yes vote tabled (set aside) an amendment to SB 1082 that would have replaced its text with constitutional protections for workplace safety, pregnancy accommodations, unpaid wage recovery and protection from harassment and retaliation.

state-nc-upper|nc-S544.meaning: A yes vote tabled (set aside) an amendment to HB 1089 that would have authorized a higher property tax rate on residences valued at $2 million or more and exempted it from the levy limit.

state-nc-upper|nc-S545.meaning: A yes vote tabled (set aside) an amendment to HB 1089 that would have required property tax exemptions for residents aged 65 or older, disabled veterans and first-time homebuyers.

state-nc-upper|nc-S546.meaning: A yes vote tabled (set aside) an amendment to HB 1089 that would have required the levy limit to include exceptions to fund public schools and public safety services.

state-nc-upper|nc-S557.meaning: A yes vote overrode the Governor's veto of HB 87, which elects North Carolina to take part in the federal tax credit for contributions to scholarship granting organizations.

state-nc-upper|nc-S569.meaning: A yes vote tabled (set aside) an amendment to HB 301 that would have enacted the North Carolina Consumer Privacy Act as a new Chapter 75F of the General Statutes.

state-nj-upper|nj-s1446-s-2024-06-28-con.meaning: A yes vote accepted the governor's conditional veto of S 1446, the first-generation and first-time homebuyer down payment assistance bill, which adds an $8 million Affordable Housing Trust Fund appropriation to the program.

state-nj-upper|nj-s3620-s-2025-03-24-con.meaning: A yes vote concurred in Assembly floor amendments to S 3620 that redefine smart meter and replace above-average usage alerts with text or email notices, on the 10th and 20th day of each billing cycle, of usage cost and amount.

state-nj-upper|nj-a3361-s-2025-06-30-con.meaning: A yes vote accepted the governor's conditional veto of A 3361, raising the cap on annual rent increases for manufactured-home park tenants from 3% to 3.5% and requiring landlords seeking larger increases to give tenants proof of need.

state-nj-upper|nj-a5267-s-2025-06-30-ame.meaning: A yes vote adopted Senate floor amendments to A 5267 that move up the Board of Public Utilities' storage incentive award deadlines and cut the minimum first-round award from 500 MW to 350 MW of the 1,000 MW goal.

state-nj-upper|nj-a5267-s-2025-06-30-rec.meaning: A yes vote reconsidered the Senate's earlier passage of A 5267, the transmission-scale energy storage bill, reopening it so Senate floor amendments could be offered.

state-nj-upper|nj-a5563-s-2025-06-30-ame.meaning: A yes vote adopted Senate floor amendments to A 5563 that replace temperature-based utility shutoff protections with a ban on shutoffs from June 15 to August 31 and require service restored June 15 without a reconnection fee.

state-nj-upper|nj-s4293-s-2025-06-30-con.meaning: A yes vote concurred in the Assembly floor amendment to S 4293, the data center water and energy usage report bill, which directs the Board of Public Utilities to consult and coordinate with the Department of Environmental Protection.

state-nj-upper|nj-s4530-s-2025-06-30-con.meaning: A yes vote concurred in Assembly floor amendments to S 4530, the community solar bill, moving the 3,000 MW solicitation registration deadline from August 1 to October 1, 2025 and removing a rulemaking requirement for utility-owned projects.

state-nj-upper|nj-a2090-s-2025-12-22-ame.meaning: A yes vote adopted a Senate floor amendment to A 2090 exempting food waste sent to landfills that deliver landfill gas to gas-to-energy facilities for renewable energy or renewable natural gas from the bill's requirements.

state-nj-upper|nj-s3389-s-2025-12-22-con.meaning: A yes vote concurred in Assembly floor amendments to S 3389, the railroad safety bill, which allow out-of-state dangerous hazardous trains to run through New Jersey with under two crew and create a wayside detector program.

state-nj-upper|nj-a3036-s-2026-01-12-con.meaning: A yes vote accepted the governor's conditional veto of A 3036, letting the Attorney General work with navigation app operators on an alternative fix instead of only ordering reroutes, adding a retain-or-repeal recommendation, and extending rulemaking time.

state-nj-upper|nj-a3451-s-2026-01-12-con.meaning: A yes vote concurred in Assembly floor amendments to A 3451 that cut the employment needed for Family Leave Act protection from 12 months to three months and from 1,000 base hours to 250.

state-nj-upper|nj-a4973-s-2026-01-12-con.meaning: A yes vote accepted the governor's conditional veto of A 4973, the Manufactured Home Park Protection Act, exempting sales of parks that already have a written agreement, letter of intent, or other commitment on the effective date.

state-nj-upper|nj-a4978-s-2026-01-12-con.meaning: A yes vote accepted the governor's conditional veto of A 4978, limiting the shootings data prosecutors must report to crimes in which a firearm was discharged without causing bodily injury.

state-nj-upper|nj-a6201-s-2026-01-12-con.meaning: A yes vote concurred in Assembly floor amendments to A 6201 removing State Health Benefits Plan language that adjusted or eliminated cost-savings proposals lacking verified savings and required the State to reimburse carriers' implementation costs.

state-nj-upper|nj-a6309-s-2026-01-12-con.meaning: A yes vote accepted the governor's conditional veto of A 6309, allowing data requests for professional licensure, making government agencies rather than employees liable, and having the Health Department enforce against health care facilities.

state-nj-upper|nj-s3802-s-2026-01-12-con.meaning: A yes vote concurred in Assembly amendments to S 3802, the recycled plastic construction materials bill, adding exemptions where compliant materials are unavailable within 60 days of construction start and for deed-restricted affordable housing.

state-nj-upper|nj-s4510-s-2026-01-12-con.meaning: A yes vote concurred in Assembly floor amendments to S 4510, the contested child custody bill, adding child abuse history and siblings' safety as custody factors and tightening rules on court-ordered reunification therapy.

state-nj-upper|nj-s4733-s-2026-01-12-con.meaning: A yes vote concurred in the Assembly amendment to S 4733, the $45 million Palisades Interstate Park Commission appropriation, requiring the funds be spent under Transportation Trust Fund expenditure requirements.

state-nj-upper|nj-s4834-s-2026-01-12-con.meaning: A yes vote concurred in Assembly floor amendments to S 4834, the motorized bicycle bill, removing scooter operators from the pedestrian injury coverage definition and delaying that coverage section's effective date to the 12th month after enactment.

state-nj-upper|nj-s4835-s-2026-01-12-con.meaning: A yes vote concurred in Assembly amendments to S 4835, the mail-in ballot cure bill, adding supervisory review before ballot rejection, limits on challengers, cure recording, and a July 1, 2026 effective date contingent on certification.

state-nj-upper|nj-s4847-s-2026-01-12-con.meaning: A yes vote concurred in the Assembly floor amendment to S 4847, the Cannabis Regulatory Commission bill, making meetings attended by more than two members, rather than one, subject to the Open Public Meetings Act.

state-nj-upper|nj-s4928-s-2026-01-12-con.meaning: A yes vote concurred in the Assembly amendment to S 4928, the data center prevailing wage bill, limiting it to data center construction projects that begin on or after its effective date.

state-nj-upper|nj-s3522-s-2026-02-24-ame.meaning: A yes vote adopted Senate floor amendments to S 3522 letting government entities share automated license plate reader information with other jurisdictions' law enforcement for criminal investigations if the agency certifies it will follow use terms.

state-sc-upper|sc-s-25088.meaning: A yes vote tabled Senator Massey's Amendment 27 to S 62, which would have required eligible students to have attended a South Carolina public school for at least ninety days the previous year.

state-sc-upper|sc-s-25100.meaning: A yes vote tabled Senator Sabb's Amendment 39 to S 62, which would have let the Education Department's vendor-contracting authority for the scholarship program expire after three years unless the General Assembly extended it.

state-sc-upper|sc-s-25105.meaning: A yes vote tabled Senator Graham's Amendment 41 to S 62, which would have barred the department from accepting new first-year scholarship applicants until January 15, 2027.

state-sc-upper|sc-s-25207.meaning: A yes vote tabled Senator Sabb's Amendment 4A to S 28, which would have set a maximum ten-year sentence for a first offense and two to ten years for later offenses.

state-sc-upper|sc-s-25331.meaning: A yes vote would have tabled Senator Goldfinch's Amendment 1A to S 244, which rewrote how juries assign fault to non-parties and deleted the bill's Sections 1.B, 1.C and 1.D.

state-sc-upper|sc-s-25707.meaning: A yes vote would have tabled Senator Davis's Amendment 2 to H 3309, which would have removed the 125-acre footprint test, leaving only the 75-megawatt capacity test, from the generating-plant definition in Section 58-33-20(2)(a).

state-sc-upper|sc-s-25749.meaning: A yes vote tabled Senator Massey's Amendment 20B to H 3309, which would have let nonresidential customers using at least 100 kilowatts buy electricity from third-party suppliers.

state-sc-upper|sc-s-25817.meaning: A yes vote adopted Senator Hembree's Amendment RFH-1 to S 62, a multi-part rewrite that, among other changes, set the income cap at 500 percent of poverty from 2026-27 and created a state-appointed trustee for the scholarship fund.

state-sc-upper|sc-s-25970.meaning: A yes vote would have tabled Senator Climer's Amendment 17A to H 4025, which would have directed the state to seek a federal waiver barring SNAP purchases of candy and soft drinks.

state-sc-upper|sc-s-25973.meaning: A yes vote adopted Senator Martin's Amendment 36 to H 4025, which raised the figure in budget proviso 91.13 on in-district compensation for legislators from $1,000 to $2,500.

state-sc-upper|sc-s-25993.meaning: A yes vote tabled Senator Martin's Amendment RFH-2 to S 62, which would have sent the scholarship fund's money to the general fund if the program ended and routed education lottery ticket revenue first to existing programs.

state-sc-upper|sc-s-26012.meaning: A yes vote tabled Senator Ott's Amendment RFH-7 to S 62, which would have limited the scholarship program to fifteen thousand students in 2026-27 and later years.

state-sc-upper|sc-s-26014.meaning: A yes vote tabled Senator Ott's Amendment RFH-9 to S 62, which would have limited administrative costs taken from the scholarship fund, including the trustee's fee, to two percent.

state-sc-upper|sc-s-26016.meaning: A yes vote tabled Senator Ott's Amendment 12 to S 62, which would have barred the fund's trustee from holding a direct financial interest in any entity receiving scholarship money.

state-sc-upper|sc-s-26022.meaning: A yes vote tabled Senator Matthews's Amendment 1 to H 3862, which would have changed the cap on military dependents' share of a charter school's enrollment to five percent.

state-sc-upper|sc-s-26094.meaning: A yes vote tabled Senator Hutto's Amendment 1 to H 3996, which would have raised to four the number of anesthesiologist's assistants one anesthesiologist could supervise, and barred CRNAs from supervising assistant students.

state-sc-upper|sc-s-26204.meaning: A yes vote concurred in the House amendments to H 3309, the South Carolina Energy Security Act, sending the bill to be enrolled as an Act.

state-sc-upper|sc-s-26311.meaning: A yes vote closed debate on S 318 under Senate Rule 15A, limiting it to two more amendments before a vote on the Commission on Fiscal Restraint and Government Efficiency resolution.

state-sc-lower|sc-h-26410.meaning: A yes vote tabled Amendment 16 to H 4760, which would have allowed rape, incest and domestic-violence survivors to receive prescriptions by telemedicine without further verification of survivor status.

state-sc-lower|sc-h-26412.meaning: A yes vote tabled Amendment 18 to H 4760, which would have rewritten the civil-action section so injured women could sue those who illegally provided abortion-inducing drugs, but never be liable themselves.

state-sc-lower|sc-h-26423.meaning: A yes vote tabled a motion to reconsider the earlier vote tabling Amendment 2 to H 4759, the hemp regulation substitute, so that vote stood.

state-sc-lower|sc-h-26424.meaning: A yes vote would have tabled a motion to reconsider the earlier vote tabling the motion to recommit H 4759, which would have kept the bill from being recommitted.

state-sc-lower|sc-h-26425.meaning: A yes vote sent H 4759, the intoxicating hemp products bill, back to the Judiciary Committee, removing it from House floor consideration.

state-sc-lower|sc-h-26454.meaning: A yes vote tabled Amendment 4 to H 4755, which would have had the Governor appoint the Judicial Merit Selection Commission on named legal groups' recommendations and barred legislators and their relatives from serving.

state-sc-lower|sc-h-26487.meaning: A yes vote tabled Amendment 4 to H 4757, which would have let a parent appeal the State Board's final decision to the Administrative Law Court before suing the school district.

state-sc-lower|sc-h-26490.meaning: A yes vote adopted Amendment 23 to H 4757, which lets a parent file documentation designating that the physician use evidence-based judgment on the child's care, with that authorization lasting until revoked.

state-sc-lower|sc-h-26544.meaning: A yes vote tabled Amendment 3 to H 4762, which would have let public schools also display Frederick Douglass's 1852 speech "What to the Slave is the Fourth of July?"

state-sc-lower|sc-h-26546.meaning: A yes vote tabled Amendment 6 to H 4762, which would have let public schools also display the Reconstruction Acts and highlights of the era, such as the first Black legislators.

state-sc-lower|sc-h-26547.meaning: A yes vote would have tabled a motion for cloture, which limits debate, on H 4762, the volunteer chaplain and historical displays bill.

state-sc-lower|sc-h-26549.meaning: A yes vote tabled Amendment 7 to H 4762, which would have let public schools also display a document on Ida B. Wells's anti-lynching journalism.

state-sc-lower|sc-h-26550.meaning: A yes vote tabled Amendment 8 to H 4762, which would have let public schools also display the Letter from Birmingham Jail, the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Voting Rights Act of 1965.

state-sc-lower|sc-h-26551.meaning: A yes vote tabled Amendment 9 to H 4762, which would have let public schools also display documents on Black women's contributions, including Sojourner Truth, Shirley Chisholm and Fannie Lou Hamer.

state-sc-lower|sc-h-26552.meaning: A yes vote tabled Amendment 10 to H 4762, which would have let public schools also display a document on Robert Smalls and his role in South Carolina public education.

state-sc-lower|sc-h-26553.meaning: A yes vote tabled Amendment 11 to H 4762, which would have let public schools also display documents on Gullah Geechee culture and its heritage contributions.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250326-018.meaning: A yes vote would have added fascism alongside communism to SB 24's social studies instruction, including contrasting both ideologies with U.S. founding principles and covering modern threats from fascist regimes.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250331-023.meaning: A yes vote would have exempted food and drink items produced, processed or manufactured in Texas from SB 379's ban on buying certain items with SNAP benefits.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250331-022.meaning: A yes vote would have exempted SNAP recipients living in a defined "food desert" from SB 379's ban on using benefits to buy sweetened drinks, candy, chips and similar items.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250401-026.meaning: A yes vote would have removed SB 8's under-one-million population limit, so sheriffs of counties of any size with an ICE agreement could apply for the state grant program.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250401-025.meaning: A yes vote would have let a sheriff terminate an SB 8 ICE agreement if a state grant was not awarded or did not substantially cover costs, and barred attorney general suits against such a sheriff.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250401-024.meaning: A yes vote would have excused a sheriff from SB 8's required ICE agreement unless the comptroller had disclosed the sheriff's grant amount to the county, or the sheriff declined or was ineligible for a grant.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250401-012.meaning: A yes vote would have limited SB 965's protection for school employees' religious speech or prayer to on-duty time other than instructional time.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250402-027.meaning: A yes vote would have added to SB 689 changes to Texas employment-discrimination law, including extending the complaint filing deadline from 180 days to two years and allowing punitive damages against governmental entities.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250402-026.meaning: A yes vote would have added to SB 689 a provision that its ban on diversity offices does not limit state agencies' duties or authority under Government Code Chapter 2161, the historically underutilized business program.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250402-025.meaning: A yes vote adopted an amendment to SB 689 barring governmental entities from requiring or soliciting diversity, equity and inclusion statements, or giving preferential consideration based on providing one.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250403-013.meaning: A yes vote adopted an amendment to SB 2188 extending its beach-closure authority for space flight activities to a municipality's mayor, who must also meet the holiday approval and closure-restriction rules.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250408-009.meaning: A yes vote would have required school districts and charter schools under SB 609 to implement required policies "in good faith" rather than simply to implement them.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250409-025.meaning: A yes vote would have capped at 10 percent a year any premium increase for an auto or home policyholder whose appraisal exceeded the insurer's last offer by 25 percent or more, with limited exceptions.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250410-041.meaning: A yes vote would have restored, in SB 1871, out-of-school suspension of students below grade three for conduct with the elements of a violent offense under Penal Code 22.01, 22.011, 22.02 or 22.021, instead of classroom disruption.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250414-006.meaning: A yes vote would have removed from SB 326 the requirement that schools and colleges use the examples referenced in the state's antisemitism definition when deciding whether discipline-worthy conduct was motivated by antisemitism.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250414-004.meaning: A yes vote would have added to SB 1596, which removes short-barrel firearms from the prohibited-weapons offense, a rule that they may be transferred only through a licensed dealer's background check, and kept their definition.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250414-001.meaning: A yes vote adopted an amendment to SB 762 removing foreign-country flags from those schools may display, changing "state flag" to "Texas flag," and barring display of permitted flags altered in color, symbols or appearance.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250415-033.meaning: A yes vote would have added to SB 37 a Texas Scholars tuition assistance program, capped at $500 million a year, for top-10-percent high school graduates entering the highest-rated degree programs.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250416-026.meaning: A yes vote would have removed from SB 30 the provision making Workers' Compensation Division treatment guidelines and drug formularies admissible as evidence on the necessity of health care services.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250416-025.meaning: A yes vote would have struck SB 30's claimant disclosure requirements, covering provider invoices, letters of protection, provider refund agreements and attorney-referral information in health care expense cases.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250416-024.meaning: A yes vote would have replaced SB 30's 300-percent-of-Medicare ceiling on provable health care charges with a "usual and customary rate" ceiling and removed its clean-claim invoice requirement.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250416-023.meaning: A yes vote would have removed SB 30's new statutory definitions of "physical pain and suffering" and "mental or emotional pain or anguish."

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250422-011.meaning: A yes vote would have required the governor's office, in SB 825's study, to count both state money spent on services for unauthorized immigrants and the money they contribute to state revenue and the economy.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250423-015.meaning: A yes vote would have added to SB 240 protection from discipline or civil liability for out-of-state licensed providers who prescribe or mail FDA-approved drugs by telehealth to patients in Texas.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250424-020.meaning: A yes vote concurred in the House amendments to SB 2, which cap education savings account spending at $1 billion for 2025-27 and order application priority by sibling status and household income.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250424-005.meaning: A yes vote would have added to SB 1349 an offense for agents of foreign governments or terrorist organizations who knowingly spread materially false information to influence opinion or suppress dissent.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250428-034.meaning: A yes vote would have let school boards appoint district-employed teachers, counselors and administrators as voting members of local school health advisory councils, instead of only as nonvoting advisers, in SB 1395.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250428-030.meaning: A yes vote would have conditioned SB 1718's major events reimbursement funding for National Rifle Association events on the event providing equal time and space for gun control advocates.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250429-041.meaning: A yes vote would have struck SB 2722's requirement that counties of four million or more allocate at least 95 percent of retained toll revenue among commissioners precincts by share of county-maintained roads.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250429-004.meaning: A yes vote would have created a teacher student-loan repayment program in SB 2253: up to $5,000 yearly for five years for certified teachers with three years' service, plus $2,500 for shortage fields.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250430-033.meaning: A yes vote would have struck SB 2330's changes to municipal meet-and-confer law, which tie those agreements to the bill's ban on payroll deduction of labor-organization dues.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250430-031.meaning: A yes vote would have added a temporary Mexican guest-worker program to SB 324 and delayed its E-verify mandates until the earlier of a Workforce Commission finding of enough guest workers or September 1, 2029.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250430-030.meaning: A yes vote would have added to SB 324 that nothing in its E-verify requirements requires firing an employee over an E-verify report or authorizes firing a legally authorized worker based on one.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250507-035.meaning: A yes vote concurred in the House amendment to SB 530, which adds a duty for the Higher Education Coordinating Board to act so each institution is accredited as federal student aid requires.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250507-030.meaning: A yes vote adopted an amendment to SB 986 making a public information officer ineligible to serve as one for the governmental body if the attorney general finds the officer sought an attorney general decision in bad faith.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250507-027.meaning: A yes vote would have added to SB 1999 that public employers may not discipline or retaliate against an employee for listing or displaying preferred pronouns, while keeping the harassment carve-out.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250508-020.meaning: A yes vote adopted an amendment to SB 2337 treating a proxy advisory service as not solely in shareholders' financial interest if it rests on nonfinancial factors like ESG or DEI, or opposes board advice without an economic analysis.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250512-048.meaning: A yes vote would have required districts to obtain a parent's written consent, requested separately at least 14 days ahead, before a student receives SB 205's fetal development instruction.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-R-20250512-046.meaning: A yes vote adopted an amendment limiting SB 1835's resident-tuition rule for nonresident scholarship students to U.S. citizens, permanent residents, nonimmigrant visa holders and others lawfully present.

state-ky-upper|ky-s-26rs-4102.meaning: A yes vote concurred in House Floor Amendment 2 to SB 251, which requires any Department of Corrections execution-protocol policy to be posted publicly on its website, and passed the bill finally.

state-md-lower|md-25h107.meaning: A yes vote adopted the previous question on HB 161 at third reading, ending debate so the House could vote on passing the bill.

state-md-lower|md-25h124.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Delegate Hornberger's amendment to HB 424 requiring the board's upper payment limits to include a waiver process for drugs in shortage, WHO-listed essential medicines, or medically necessary for continuity of care.

state-md-lower|md-25h123.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Delegate Pippy's amendment to HB 424 requiring the Legislative Policy Committee to approve the board's upper-payment-limit process, and barring limits until it approves.

state-md-lower|md-25h122.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Delegate Hartman's amendment to HB 424 exempting FDA-designated orphan drugs from the upper payment limit provisions unless an alternative equivalent treatment exists.

state-md-lower|md-25h120.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Delegate Buckel's amendment to HB 424 requiring the board to study effects on the State biotechnic industry before setting a new upper payment limit.

state-md-lower|md-25h119.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Delegate Buckel's amendment to HB 424 requiring the board to certify that upper payment limits will not reduce patient access and to consult patient advocacy groups.

state-md-lower|md-25h194.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Delegate Schmidt's amendment to HB 6 requiring a physical inspection when a property owner appeals an assessment made with oblique aerial imagery, and requiring notices to say if imagery was used.

state-md-lower|md-25h273.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Delegate Fisher's amendment to HB 504 letting students in failing schools attend an alternative school, including through a new scholarship program and military boarding school options.

state-md-lower|md-25h268.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Delegate Miller's amendment to HB 1380 extending perinatal care standards and new perinatal palliative care protocols to reproductive health care providers other than hospitals and birthing centers.

state-md-lower|md-25h267.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Delegate Buckel's amendment to HB 1424 striking the Attorney General powers and other provisions the Appropriations Committee amendments had added to the bill.

state-md-lower|md-25h265.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Delegate R. Long's amendment to HB 339 making a tenant responsible for the utility bill for air-conditioning, unless the lease says otherwise.

state-md-lower|md-25h440.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Delegate Adams's amendment to HB 23 letting a taxpayer appeal to the Maryland Tax Court if a county exceeds the special property tax rate limit, with a damages award if the taxpayer wins.

state-md-lower|md-25h450.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Delegate Miller's amendment to HB 930 requiring entities receiving grants under the program to complete human trafficking prevention training from the University of Maryland SAFE Center.

state-md-lower|md-25h449.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Delegate Tomlinson's amendment to HB 930 changing the grant program's wording from "individuals in" to "residents of".

state-md-lower|md-25h446.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Delegate Wivell's amendment to HB 930 requiring physicians and certain facilities that perform abortions to report to the Maryland Department of Health and the federal CDC.

state-md-lower|md-25h545.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Delegate Chisholm's amendment to HB 49 adding grocery stores and supermarkets to the list of building types in the committee amendments.

state-md-lower|md-25h1355.meaning: A yes vote concurred in the Senate's amendments to HB 1046, which concerns technical service bulletins in mechanical repair contracts, and gave the bill final passage.

state-md-lower|md-25h1354.meaning: A yes vote concurred in the Senate's amendments to HB 1020, which governs credit reporting of medical debt, and gave the bill final passage.

state-md-lower|md-25h1352.meaning: A yes vote concurred in the Senate's amendments to HB 861, which requires transportation network companies to provide weekly fare and earnings summaries, and gave the bill final passage.

state-md-lower|md-25h1350.meaning: A yes vote concurred in the Senate's amendments to HB 1078, which concerns the Federal Bureau of Investigation headquarters in Prince George's County, and gave the bill final passage.

state-md-lower|md-25h1347.meaning: A yes vote concurred in the Senate's amendments to HB 717, which concerns acquisition, staffing, operations, and funding for public lands, and gave the bill final passage.

state-md-lower|md-25h1345.meaning: A yes vote concurred in the Senate's amendments to HB 1173, which authorizes speed monitoring systems on high-risk highways in Montgomery County, and gave the bill final passage.

state-md-lower|md-25h1341.meaning: A yes vote concurred in the Senate's amendments to HB 1123, which changes medical and elder parole, and gave the bill final passage.

state-md-lower|md-25h1337.meaning: A yes vote concurred in the Senate's amendments to HB 15, which authorizes limited worker cooperative associations, and gave the bill final passage.

state-md-lower|md-25h1334.meaning: A yes vote concurred in the Senate's amendments to HB 774, which alters the Hunger-Free Campus Grant Program, and gave the bill final passage.

state-md-lower|md-25h1333.meaning: A yes vote concurred in the Senate's amendments to HB 599, which concerns collective bargaining for the BWI Airport Fire and Rescue Department, and gave the bill final passage.

state-md-lower|md-25h1332.meaning: A yes vote concurred in the Senate's amendments to HB 502, which concerns the Office of Disability Employment Advancement and Policy and Maryland as a model employer, and gave the bill final passage.

state-md-lower|md-25h1329.meaning: A yes vote concurred in the Senate's amendments to HB 913, which authorizes speed monitoring systems on Interstate 83 in Baltimore City, and gave the bill final passage.

state-md-lower|md-25h1328.meaning: A yes vote concurred in the Senate's amendments to HB 716, which concerns the Statewide Rental Assistance Voucher Program, and gave the bill final passage.

state-md-lower|md-25h1322.meaning: A yes vote concurred in the Senate's amendments to HB 974, which sets enforcement authority for preventive services in health insurance, and gave the bill final passage.

state-md-lower|md-25h1319.meaning: A yes vote concurred in the Senate's amendments to HB 424, which concerns the Prescription Drug Affordability Board's authority for upper payment limits, and gave the bill final passage.

state-md-lower|md-25h1313.meaning: A yes vote adopted the conference committee report on HB 292, which concerns funding for cooperative housing corporations, condominiums, and homeowners associations, and gave the bill final passage.

state-md-lower|md-25h1311.meaning: A yes vote ended debate and brought to a vote the adoption of the conference committee report on HB 352, the Budget Reconciliation and Financing Act of 2025.

state-md-lower|md-25h1309.meaning: A yes vote would have made the conference committee report on HB 350, the Fiscal Year 2026 Budget Bill, a special order for later consideration instead of voting on it then.

state-md-lower|md-25h1276.meaning: A yes vote passed SB 365, which establishes a Nonprofit Organizations Navigator in the Department of Commerce, on third reading.

state-md-lower|md-26h34.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Delegate Schmidt's amendment to HB 488, replacing the congressional map with a rule barring the General Assembly, absent a court order, from redistricting Congress more than once every 10 years after a census.

state-md-lower|md-26h33.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Delegate M. Morgan's amendment to HB 488, striking from the bill the wording of the ballot question to be put to voters on the constitutional amendment.

state-md-lower|md-26h32.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Delegate Buckel's amendment to HB 444, allowing immigration enforcement agreements for civil immigration enforcement when a person was convicted and sentenced to more than 180 days of incarceration.

state-md-lower|md-26h31.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Delegate Griffith's amendment to HB 444, allowing immigration enforcement agreements for civil immigration enforcement when a person has been charged with murder or rape.

state-md-lower|md-26h30.meaning: A yes vote would have amended HB 444 to let the State or local governments enter immigration enforcement agreements when an individual is charged with first-degree child abuse.

state-md-lower|md-26h29.meaning: A yes vote would have amended HB 444 to allow immigration enforcement agreements when an individual is charged with a first- or second-degree sexual offense, or sexual abuse of a minor in certain circumstances.

state-md-lower|md-26h28.meaning: A yes vote would have amended HB 444 to allow immigration enforcement agreements when an individual has been charged with a crime of violence.

state-md-lower|md-26h43.meaning: A yes vote would have replaced HB 444's prohibition on immigration enforcement agreements with a requirement that correctional facilities, when federal authorities request, give 48 hours' notice of an individual's release and transfer the individual to federal immigration authorities.

state-md-lower|md-26h58.meaning: A yes vote would have sent HB 1, limiting cost recovery by investor-owned utilities, back to committee (a motion to recommit).

state-md-lower|md-26h57.meaning: A yes vote would have amended HB 1 to bar raising the pay of a Public Service Commission commissioner or certain senior commission officials without General Assembly approval.

state-md-lower|md-26h72.meaning: A yes vote would have amended HB 226 to bar officials, employees, and their immediate family members of the Department of Disabilities from serving in or running an affiliated foundation.

state-md-lower|md-26h145.meaning: A yes vote would have amended HB 1017 to declare that its provisions are not severable, so if any part were struck down no other part would take effect.

state-md-lower|md-26h144.meaning: A yes vote would have amended HB 351 to let prosecutors apply for a warrant to gather and securely retain identifying digital data about a judicial officer who is the subject of a misconduct complaint.

state-md-lower|md-26h143.meaning: A yes vote would have amended HB 351 to allow a legal action under the bill only after a final determination of a rights violation by an internal investigation office or independent authority, and after appeals.

state-md-lower|md-26h142.meaning: A yes vote would have amended a Judiciary Committee amendment to HB 351 by striking the words "or allows" from its text.

state-md-lower|md-26h290.meaning: A yes vote would have amended HB 437 so a highway-capacity impact assessment could not delay construction, and so the Department must prioritize congestion relief, safety, and efficient movement of people and goods.

state-md-lower|md-26h289.meaning: A yes vote would have amended HB 437 to change greenhouse-gas "offsetting" to "mitigating" and to require the Department to publish estimated net emissions and mitigation options for major highway projects.

state-md-lower|md-26h288.meaning: A yes vote would have postponed floor consideration of HB 306, on prices listed on dealer websites, until March 12 (a motion to special order).

state-md-lower|md-26h408.meaning: A yes vote would have postponed floor consideration of HB 543, on family child care homes in landlord-tenant law, until March 18 (a motion to special order).

state-md-lower|md-26h404.meaning: A yes vote would have amended HB 1532 to repeal the environmental surcharge on electric customers' bills and bar gas and electric companies from imposing certain cost-recovery surcharges, taxes, or fees.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-1-20250812-005.meaning: A yes vote would have narrowed SB 14's required officer department file to documents on alleged misconduct the agency found insufficiently supported, dropping the requirement to include any other letter, memo or document about the officer.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-2-20250818-021.meaning: A yes vote would have exempted payments under contracts made before SB 13's effective date from its lobbying spending ban and struck the provision voiding contract terms for prohibited payments.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-2-20250818-020.meaning: A yes vote would have let an individual file a sworn Texas Ethics Commission complaint alleging a violation of SB 13's lobbying spending ban, with the commission able to impose a penalty.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-2-20250818-019.meaning: A yes vote would have loosened SB 13's exceptions so employees could advocate on legislation regardless of lobbyist-registration rules, and any association employee could tell legislators how a pending matter affects a subdivision.

state-tx-upper|tx-s-2-20250818-018.meaning: A yes vote would have exempted from SB 13's ban on spending public funds on lobbyists any political subdivision activity related to emergency management, disaster response, or public health and safety.

state-ut-lower|ut-2026GS-H1249.meaning: A yes vote accepted the Senate's two amendments to HB 209, which changed the registration form's citizenship notice from "on the back of" to "with" the form and made a technical edit to a private-records list.

state-ut-lower|ut-2026GS-H1282.meaning: A yes vote accepted the Senate's amendments to HB 381, which bar operating motor assisted scooters and high power electric devices on a freeway, and bar riders under 16 from operating personal electric vehicles on one.

state-ut-lower|ut-2026GS-H1300.meaning: A yes vote accepted the Senate's substitute for HB 502, which adds a parent's right to opt a student out of citizenship grading; an opted-out student is ineligible for the citizenship scholarship.

state-ut-lower|ut-2026GS-H1318.meaning: A yes vote accepted the Senate's substitute for HB 565, which added retrospective operation to January 1, 2026 for the requirement that counties separately state city library levies on property tax notices.

state-ut-lower|ut-2026GS-H1359.meaning: A yes vote accepted the Senate's amendment to HB 366, which lets a municipality and its judicial district's presiding judge agree by memorandum of understanding to a different arrangement for managing the municipality's municipal cases.

state-ut-lower|ut-2026GS-H1408.meaning: A yes vote reconsidered the House's third-reading passage of SB 267, reopening the bill; a floor amendment striking "targeted" before "advertising" in a list of student protections was then adopted.

state-ut-lower|ut-2026GS-H1433.meaning: A yes vote accepted the Senate's substitute for HB 514, which requires the State Finance Review Commission to approve energy infrastructure district revenue bonds before issuance and creates an Enterprise Fund in place of a Revenue Fund.

state-ut-lower|ut-2026GS-H1613.meaning: A yes vote accepted the Senate's substitute for HB 111, which adds a Poaching Mitigation Fund fed by restitution money and changes guide and outfitter definitions, fees and use of the Guide and Outfitter Fund.

state-ut-upper|ut-2025GS-S607.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted a Senate floor amendment to SB 212 allowing a person's failure to wear protective headgear to be introduced as evidence in civil litigation on negligence, injuries or mitigation of damages.

state-ut-upper|ut-2025GS-S1876.meaning: A yes vote accepted the House's amendments to SB 277, which add a survey every two years, starting in 2027, by the Division of Human Resource Management on the Government Records Office director's job performance.

state-ut-upper|ut-2025GS-S1885.meaning: A yes vote accepted the House's amendments to SB 203, which require the third party, not the plaintiff, to meet standing requirements, and for association suits require that any member meet standing and consent.

state-ut-upper|ut-2025GS-S1889.meaning: A yes vote accepted the House's amendments to SB 333, which drop the creating entity's authority to impose municipal energy and telecommunications taxes in a venue zone and limit a county's resort communities tax to unincorporated areas.

state-ut-upper|ut-2025GS-S1955.meaning: A yes vote accepted the House's amendments to SB 73, which require publishing the initiative application rather than the petition and add special effective dates for parts of the bill.

state-ut-upper|ut-2025GS-S2157.meaning: A yes vote accepted the House's amendments to SB 234, which replace the mining-exploration severance tax credit with an agreement-based certificate process, schedule its repeal after legislative review, and allow a high cost infrastructure credit against 2025 severance tax.

state-ut-upper|ut-2025GS-S2170.meaning: A yes vote accepted the House's amendments to SB 197, which raise renter's credit income limits and maximum amounts and require homeowner's credit or indigent abatement receipt within the previous two years, beginning in 2026.

state-ut-upper|ut-2026GS-S1366.meaning: A yes vote accepted the House's amendment to SB 131, which removes the COVID-19 emergency definition and an obsolete 2022-2023 school-year charter enrollment priority.

state-ut-upper|ut-2026GS-S1699.meaning: A yes vote accepted the House's substitute for SB 153, which changes who prepares the ballot title and analysis for a proposed constitutional amendment, and adds coordination clauses with H.B. 209 and H.B. 361.

state-ut-upper|ut-2026GS-S1791.meaning: A yes vote accepted the House's amendments to SB 186, which cut its appropriation from $15,995,000 to $3,600,000, remove charter school educational service agencies, and add an oath of office for charter school governing board members.

state-ut-upper|ut-2026GS-S1857.meaning: A yes vote accepted the House's amendments to SB 229, which limit the state paid time off program to new employees and current employees who elect it, and require each agency to run a leave bank program.

state-ut-upper|ut-2026GS-S1969.meaning: A yes vote accepted the House's floor amendment to SB 324, which replaces the Office of the Legislative Auditor General with the Office of the Legislative Fiscal Analyst, with the governor's budget office, in setting grant evaluation standards.

state-ut-upper|ut-2026GS-S2248.meaning: A yes vote accepted the House's amendments to SB 225, which modify the authority's minimum mitigation and environmental standards, widen the property tax differential recruitment-incentive prohibition beyond capital city land, and add an immediate effective date.

state-ut-upper|ut-2026GS-S2256.meaning: A yes vote accepted the House's amendment to SB 170, which removes the requirement that a parent sign an acknowledgment form, kept in the medical record, to decline vitamin K for a newborn.

state-wv-lower|wv-h2026-00712.meaning: A yes vote would have tabled, setting aside without a vote, the amendment then pending on HB 5537, the bill repealing obsolete education code sections.

state-wv-lower|wv-h2026-00716.meaning: A yes vote adopted Delegate Burkhammer's amendment to HB 5537 requiring county superintendents to report suspected abuse of a child in imminent danger directly to Centralized Intake when a parent is withdrawing the child from school.

state-wv-upper|wv-s2025-02-18-0008.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted an amendment to SB 460 letting private, parochial and church schools and child care centers keep requiring childhood immunizations when consistent with their religious beliefs.

state-wv-upper|wv-s2025-02-18-0009.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Senator Weld's amendment to SB 460 changing "a public education" to "an education" in the bill's finding about children's right to schooling.

state-wv-upper|wv-s2025-02-18-0011.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Senator Garcia's amendment to SB 460 requiring schools and child care centers to keep and post online an annual report of how many students have vaccine exemptions, without personal information.

state-wv-upper|wv-s2025-03-07-0076.meaning: A yes vote would have replaced the committee substitute for SB 565 with text barring optometrists from using therapeutic lasers and sending any request to expand their scope to a legislative committee.

state-wv-upper|wv-s2025-03-07-0077.meaning: A yes vote adopted Senator Takubo's amendments to SB 565 requiring laser-procedure certification training to include proctored, supervised cases, at least 10 of each new procedure and 50 collective cases per person.

state-wv-upper|wv-s2025-03-14-0118.meaning: A yes vote would have replaced SB 526 with a Pharmacist Prescribing Authority Act limited to non-controlled drugs for self-limiting conditions confirmed by a waived test, with notice to the patient's primary care provider.

state-wv-upper|wv-s2025-03-31-0244.meaning: A yes vote referred SB 506, on enhanced pay for certain teachers, to the Senate Rules Committee instead of proceeding with its third-reading vote.

state-wv-upper|wv-s2025-04-01-0266.meaning: A yes vote referred SB 745, on lobbying requirements, to the Senate Rules Committee instead of proceeding with its third-reading vote.

state-wv-upper|wv-s2025-04-03-0304.meaning: A yes vote would have replaced HB 2172 with a rewrite of the Board of Physical Therapy membership section: seven members, with one of the five physical therapists dual-certified as an athletic trainer.

state-wv-upper|wv-s2025-04-08-0351.meaning: A yes vote would have amended HB 2008's committee amendment to keep economic development as a separate Department of Economic Development with its own secretary, and struck other provisions including Chapter 31G.

state-wv-upper|wv-s2025-04-08-0378.meaning: A yes vote adopted Senator Weld's amendment to HB 3017 creating a Secretary of State complaint procedure for election violations, including voting-machine inspections, requiring written, notarized, sworn complaints.

state-wv-upper|wv-s2025-04-08-0380.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Senator Oliverio's amendment to HB 3279 requiring that, by July 1, 2027, at least five lay board members come from each congressional district.

state-wv-upper|wv-s2025-04-09-0416.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Senator Takubo's amendment to HB 3444 requiring newborns to receive preventive eye ointment (tetracycline or erythromycin) at birth unless the parent opts out.

state-wv-upper|wv-s2025-04-10-0459.meaning: A yes vote concurred in the House's amendments to SB 565, the optometry practice bill, and passed it, accepting the House version with laser-certification training, adverse-outcome reporting and pediatric-patient limits.

state-wv-upper|wv-s2025-04-11-0476.meaning: A yes vote made HB 2054, the alcohol licensing and liquor sampling bill, take effect from passage rather than the usual 90 days after passage.

state-wv-upper|wv-s2025-04-11-0507.meaning: A yes vote passed HB 3492 in the Senate as rewritten by the Economic Development Committee, authorizing Huntington to levy a special district excise tax for its economic opportunity district, with an amended title.

state-wv-upper|wv-s2025-04-11-0523.meaning: A yes vote concurred in the House's amendment to HB 2008, the executive branch reorganization placing economic development as a division within the Department of Commerce, and passed the bill.

state-wv-upper|wv-s2025-04-11-0525.meaning: A yes vote concurred in the House's amendment to HB 2009, which abolishes the Department of Arts, Culture, and History and moves its sections under the Department of Tourism, and passed the bill.

state-wv-upper|wv-s2025-04-12-0552.meaning: A yes vote concurred in the House Finance Committee's amendment rewriting SB 576, which authorizes fixed odds racing in horse and dog racing, and passed the bill.

state-wv-upper|wv-s2025-04-12-0599.meaning: A yes vote concurred in the House's amendments to HB 2695, authorizing Raleigh and Mason Counties to levy special district excise taxes for economic opportunity districts, and passed the bill.

state-wv-upper|wv-s2026-01-28-0015.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Senator Woelfel's amendment to SB 388 making both the Aitken Bible and the Catholic American Bible available in the covered classrooms.

state-wv-upper|wv-s2026-02-23-0203.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Senator Martin's amendment to SB 749 adding a section abolishing economic opportunity development districts after thirty years and requiring notice and a public hearing before abolishment.

state-wv-upper|wv-s2026-02-24-0216.meaning: A yes vote would have laid SB 927, on the Commissioner of Agriculture's authority to regulate bees, over on the calendar, delaying action on it.

state-wv-upper|wv-s2026-02-26-0249.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Senator Oliverio's amendment to SB 745 exempting Class I milk and certain USDA commodity foods, such as high-protein yogurt and cheeses, from the school nutrition added-sugar limits.

state-wv-upper|wv-s2026-02-26-0250.meaning: A yes vote would have rejected SB 966, the bill changing home school instruction requirements, ending it.

state-wv-upper|wv-s2026-03-02-0270.meaning: A yes vote tabled the pending motion to withdraw SB 972 from the Health and Human Resources Committee, leaving the bill in committee.

state-wv-upper|wv-s2026-03-03-0317.meaning: A yes vote would have adopted Senator Weld's amendment to SB 1083 rewriting the indecent exposure definition, adding a breastfeeding exception, and creating a locker-room "affront or alarm" misdemeanor.

state-wv-upper|wv-s2026-03-12-0480.meaning: A yes vote passed HB 4481 in the Senate as rewritten by the Energy, Industry and Mining Committee into the Electric Load Forecast Accountability Act, with an amended title, sending it back to the House.

state-md-lower|md-25h600.meaning: A yes vote would have made people convicted of murder resulting from an act of domestic violence ineligible for HB 853's new sentence-reduction motion for those convicted at ages 18 to 24.

state-md-lower|md-25h599.meaning: A yes vote would have made people convicted of murder involving a pregnant victim ineligible for HB 853's new sentence-reduction motion for those convicted at ages 18 to 24.

state-md-lower|md-25h598.meaning: A yes vote would have made people convicted of murder of a law enforcement officer killed in the line of duty ineligible for HB 853's new sentence-reduction motion for those convicted at ages 18 to 24.

state-md-lower|md-25h596.meaning: A yes vote would have made people convicted of murder of a probation officer on duty ineligible for HB 853's new sentence-reduction motion for those convicted at ages 18 to 24.

state-md-lower|md-25h595.meaning: A yes vote would have made people convicted of murder involving more than one victim ineligible for HB 853's new sentence-reduction motion for those convicted at ages 18 to 24.

state-md-lower|md-25h594.meaning: A yes vote would have exempted immigration enforcement agreements fully executed by April 1, 2025, or under negotiation by March 31, 2025, from HB 1222's ban on State and local governments entering such agreements.

state-md-lower|md-25h593.meaning: A yes vote would have struck from HB 1222 the ban on State and local governments entering immigration enforcement agreements and the requirement to end existing ones.

state-md-lower|md-25h590.meaning: A yes vote would have cut the time a tenant has to reclaim personal property after an eviction under HB 767 from 10 days to 24 hours.

state-md-lower|md-25h589.meaning: A yes vote would have let a court award a landlord a money judgment against a tenant for the cost of storing the tenant's property after an eviction under HB 767.

state-md-lower|md-25h612.meaning: A yes vote would have required solar systems eligible under HB 1111 to contain no PFAS chemicals, adding definitions of PFAS chemicals and PFAS pesticides, along with other wording changes to the bill's eligibility terms.

state-md-lower|md-25h611.meaning: A yes vote would have required the Department to give plain-language public notice of HB 1296's managed aquifer recharge pilot program, by email and on newspaper, county and health department websites.

state-md-lower|md-25h609.meaning: A yes vote ended debate and forced an immediate vote on Delegate Buckel's amendment to HB 829, which would bar the PSC from approving an overhead transmission line until each affected county's governing body approved it.

state-md-lower|md-25h876.meaning: A yes vote would have suspended the fiscal 2026 inflation-based increase in the motor fuel tax rate, in an amendment to HB 352.

state-md-lower|md-25h875.meaning: A yes vote would have removed HB 352's changes to several vehicle registration fee sections, keeping the existing-law fee schedules for those sections.

state-md-lower|md-25h874.meaning: A yes vote would have removed HB 352's increase in the mobile sports wagering tax rate, restoring licensees' 85% share of proceeds and deleting the General Fund deposit.

state-md-lower|md-25h873.meaning: A yes vote would have removed HB 352's increase, from 50% to 90%, of the share of State property assessment costs that counties and Baltimore City must reimburse.

state-md-lower|md-25h872.meaning: A yes vote would have removed from HB 352 the requirement that certain groups of corporations file a combined (unitary) Maryland income tax return.

state-md-lower|md-25h871.meaning: A yes vote would have excluded software as a service from the sales and use tax HB 352 newly imposes on certain data and IT services and on licensing of intellectual property.

state-md-lower|md-25h870.meaning: A yes vote would have removed NAICS sector 5415 (computer systems design and related services) from the data and IT services HB 352 newly subjects to the sales and use tax.

state-md-lower|md-25h868.meaning: A yes vote would have removed from HB 352 the county share of teacher retirement costs and the changes to teacher retirement supplemental grants to counties.

state-md-lower|md-25h867.meaning: A yes vote would have removed from HB 352 the additional State income tax rate on individuals' net capital gains.

state-md-lower|md-25h866.meaning: A yes vote would have excluded the home mortgage interest deduction from HB 352's reduction of itemized deductions for filers with income above $200,000 ($100,000 if married filing separately).

state-md-lower|md-25h865.meaning: A yes vote would have required the Maryland Transportation Authority to report to the General Assembly each December 1 on bridge vulnerability assessments and on methods for future assessments, in an amendment to HB 352.

state-md-lower|md-25h864.meaning: A yes vote ended debate and forced an immediate vote on Delegate Grammer's amendment to HB 352, which would require annual Transportation Authority reports on bridge vulnerability assessments.

state-md-lower|md-25h863.meaning: A yes vote would have excluded the medical expense deduction from HB 352's reduction of itemized deductions for filers with income above $200,000 ($100,000 if married filing separately).

state-md-lower|md-25h862.meaning: A yes vote would have excluded the charitable contribution deduction from HB 352's reduction of itemized deductions for filers with income above $200,000 ($100,000 if married filing separately).

state-md-lower|md-25h860.meaning: A yes vote adopted a committee amendment to HB 352 raising the maximum county income tax rate from 3.20% to 3.30% of Maryland taxable income.

state-md-lower|md-25h858.meaning: A yes vote adopted a committee amendment to HB 352 that, among other Transportation Article changes, raised Montgomery County's Bus Rapid Transit grant floor from $20 million to $25 million and the vehicle title fee from $100 to $200.

state-md-lower|md-25h856.meaning: A yes vote adopted a committee amendment to HB 352 raising Department of Agriculture nursery inspection and certification fees and broker and dealer license fees.

state-md-lower|md-25h855.meaning: A yes vote would have added $100 million for low-income energy assistance to HB 350 and struck two $50 million clean energy appropriations for local government projects and solar on State property.

state-md-lower|md-25h854.meaning: A yes vote would have struck HB 350's contingent shift of about $10.5 million in Department of Natural Resources costs to the Chesapeake Bays Trust Fund and raised the Executive Branch general fund cut from $97 million to $129 million.

state-md-lower|md-25h853.meaning: A yes vote would have cut $760,479 from the Maryland Energy Administration's General Administration and added it to the Rural Maryland Council, contingent on legislation allowing regional greenhouse gas auction revenue for that purpose.

state-md-lower|md-25h852.meaning: A yes vote would have shifted about $3 million of Strategic Energy Investment Fund money from Energy Administration energy efficiency programs to the Rural Maryland Council, contingent on legislation authorizing it.

state-md-lower|md-25h851.meaning: A yes vote would have cut $10 million from the Governor's executive direction appropriation in HB 350, contingent on legislation restoring $10 million to the Maternal and Child Health Population Health Improvement Fund.

state-md-lower|md-25h850.meaning: A yes vote would have cut about $70.9 million from statewide personnel expenses in HB 350 and added it to provider reimbursements in the Developmental Disabilities Administration community services program.
